title: Can Mechanistic Interpretability Help Explain LLM Agent Failures? A Case Study on Web Element Hallucination
summary: Mechanistic Interpretability (MI) has made significant progress in explaining the internal computations of Large Language Models (LLMs); however, these advances have yet to demonstrate comparable success in explaining the decision-making processes of LLM-based agents. This paper examines the challenges MI tools face when applied to realistic agentic failures. We focus on one such failure: web agents hallucinating actions that are not available on a website. We apply a series of mechanistic analyzes to Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct as it interacts with live websites. We find that a linear probe trained on the last prompt token can predict hallucinations before generation begins (0.80 AUC) and steering along a probe direction corrects 85\% of hallucinations, but disrupts 7\% of valid actions. However, these results only provide a partial explanation of why the agent hallucinates. The probe direction is sensitive to prompt formatting, losing much of its steering effect after a minor change to how actions are represented. Additionally, circuit identification can be difficult as the computation is distributed across multiple components and positions, and the information the agent relies on varies across examples. We discuss how these observations challenge the assumptions underlying standard MI methods for circuit discovery and feature identification, and outline future directions for making these methods better suited to explain failures in LLM-based agents.

title: Alignment by Socialization: Learning Tradeoffs Under Selection
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents are expected to complete tasks while following rules of conduct, but these objectives can conflict. We study how evolutionary selection shapes an agent's choices between them, and whether experience can make those choices reflect human judgments and withstand subsequent pressures. In our model, copies of an agent face a common uncertain reward state, and only those taking the rewarded action reproduce. We show that long-run growth is maximized when each action is taken as often as the environment rewards it. We compare three policies. A task-only policy thrives in a sandbox rewarding completion alone but fails when conduct matters. A fixed linear policy increasingly favors task completion as its stakes rise, even where humans never reward it. A learned policy instead converges to the tradeoffs rewarded by its environment; when humans supply the rewards, we call this socialization. Accumulated experience makes socialization harder to reverse under subsequent task-only training, although violations can arise before the prevailing disposition changes, and finite memory weakens this protection. When a single violation can end a deployment, a hard prohibition can prevent it, but a mistaken prohibition can also be costly. Experiments with small neural networks illustrate how training targets and memory shape these outcomes. Our results suggest that alignment depends not only on the objectives assigned to agents, but also on the environments that shape and sustain their behavior.

title: ModHarness-RL: Recasting Harnesses as Learnable and Evolving Programs for Agentic RL
summary: Agentic reinforcement learning (RL) increasingly relies on a harness, the scaffold around the model that decides what it sees of its own interaction and what guidance it receives. Most existing approaches train under a hand-written harness that stays fixed throughout. However, an effective harness depends on the domain, the data and the model, and keeps changing as the model trains. We introduce ModHarness-RL, which recasts the harness as programs that are learned from data and evolve as the model trains with RL. ModHarness-RL records the interaction as structured State, a set of typed blocks, and two core components of the harness are programs over these blocks, a Compression program that assembles the accumulated history into the model's context and a Steering program that supplies guidance when behavior deviates. During RL training, candidate programs are proposed from recent trajectories, verified by execution, and replayed over past trajectories, so the harness tracks how the model's behavior shifts. We study CodeSearch in depth and further analyze ALFWorld and BIRD SQL, with models from 1.5B to 8B. The proposed Compression and Steering mechanisms improve held-out performance over the fixed-harness baseline in most settings. These results suggest that a harness for agentic RL can be learned from the task's data and evolved with the model.

title: Imitation Bootstrapped Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
comment: 9 pages, 5 figures. Code, videos and results: https://zhanghutony.github.io/ibmarl/. A preliminary version appeared at the PhysCollaBot Workshop at IROS 2026
summary: Demonstrations are an effective way to accelerate single-agent reinforcement learning (RL), but extending this idea to multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) is non-trivial as it is difficult and often impossible for a single person to teleoperate multiple agents simultaneously. Round-Robin Behavior Cloning (R2BC) addresses this by letting a single demonstrator control one agent at a time while the others execute their current policies. However, the resulting imitation policies are limited by the quality of the demonstrations. We propose Imitation Bootstrapped Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (IBMARL), a framework that extends Imitation Bootstrapped Reinforcement Learning (IBRL) to cooperative teams and uses R2BC to train the imitation policies. At each time step, every agent receives one action proposal from its imitation policy and one from its RL policy, and an ensemble of centralized critics selects among the per-agent combinations of the two. A gated imitation penalty, a soft Q-filtered behavior cloning loss, regularizes each RL policy toward its imitation policy only where the critics value the imitation action more, so that after training each agent executes its RL policy alone, without the centralized critics. On four cooperative multi-agent RL benchmarks, IBMARL surpasses its imitation policies $2.6$-$4.2\times$ faster than demonstration-based baselines on two tasks, is the only method to surpass it on the other two, and exceeds the demonstrator itself on two of the four. With real human demonstrations IBMARL still surpasses imitation learning alone, and does so more than twice as fast as the best baseline.

title: Adversarial Tracking: Attacks on Image Sensors for Object Tracking in Autonomous Vehicles
summary: Object tracking systems estimate the motion of surrounding vehicles by linking detected objects across video frames. In particular, Tracking-By-Detection (TBD) systems combine object detectors with motion prediction and data association to maintain object identities over time. However, neural network-based detectors are vulnerable to adversarial attacks that perturb input images, and their impact on downstream trajectory estimation is not fully characterized by detection accuracy alone. Therefore, this paper evaluates image-specific and image-agnostic attacks on YOLOv3 and YOLOv4 detectors paired with SORT, Deep SORT, Strong SORT, and OC-SORT tracking systems. The evaluation uses CARLA simulator and measures tracking quality through Multiple Object Tracking Accuracy (MOTA), Higher Order Tracking Accuracy (HOTA), and Identification F1 (IDF1). Under image-specific attacks, HOTA for YOLOv3-based trackers declines from 53.45-56.19% to 14.85-17.03%, while MOTA reaches -772.60% in the worst case. YOLOv4-based trackers exhibit greater robustness, while HOTA still declines to 25.06-26.86%. In addition, image-agnostic attacks can reduce the tracking accuracy using a single Universal Adversarial Perturbation (UAP), without generating a separate perturbation for individual frames.

title: Rethinking Visual Reasoning in Text-to-Image Reward Modeling
summary: Reward models are a core component of modern text-to-image systems, serving as the objective for inference-time selection and RL-based post-training. A key prerequisite is visual understanding: to judge prompt adherence and ground aesthetic preferences, a reward model must bind attributes, resolve relations, and count reliably. We find that widely-used reward models perform poorly on targeted visual reasoning evaluations. Even when starting from strong vision-language backbones, preference fine-tuning erodes these capabilities, and continual-learning baselines fail to mitigate a steep tradeoff between visual reasoning and preference accuracy. We propose a data-centric intervention that injects visual reasoning supervision into preference learning by flipping the pairing axis. To complement conventional human preference data (paired images under a shared prompt), we convert existing visual reasoning datasets into preference pairs that share the same image but differ in prompt, and train on the mixture. This yields a Pareto improvement in both visual understanding and preference prediction. Across inference-time best-of-n selection and RL post-training, the resulting reward model improves text-to-image generation on challenging compositional prompts (GenEval) by an average of 4.0% and 5.5% respectively, outperforming HPSv3 which was trained on 6x more preference pairs.

title: Training-Free Acceleration of Multi-View 3D Transformers via Regime-Aware Attention Approximation
summary: Multi-view 3D transformers such as VGGT reconstruct a scene from a set of unposed images in a single forward pass, predicting camera poses, depth and 3D points, but the cost of their global attention grows quadratically with the num- ber of images. Accelerators borrowed from large language models assume that each token attends to only a few oth- ers; on these models they lose accuracy or gain little speed. We study the global attention of three multi-view transform- ers on seven datasets and find that every layer plays one of three roles: it averages over the whole scene, matches points across many images, or anchors on the first image, whose coordinates the outputs use. Building on this anal- ysis, we propose Regime-AWare ATTention Approximation (RAWATTA), a training-free method that runs attention in 8- bit precision and keeps 16-bit precision only in the layers where a worst-case calibration check requires it. Its fast set- ting, RAWATTA-Fast, also approximates attention in a few averaging and anchoring layers, while matching layers and the first image keep all their keys. On a 12 GB GPU at 50 im- ages, RAWATTA runs VGGT faster than the released code, mostly through our CUDA engine, and loses at most about one point of pose accuracy (AUC@3) on any dataset; RAWATTA-Fast is slightly faster and less accurate. Both fit 200 images, where the released code runs out of memory at 100.

title: Creative Product Design under Brand Image Constraints
summary: Industrial design requires creative visual exploration while satisfying constraints that are often product-specific and implicit. Existing text-to-image (T2I) approaches can generate creative designs through concept blending or multi-agent self-enhancement, but they provide limited mechanisms for ensuring that generated designs remain consistent with such constraints. We focus on brand image as a representative design constraint and propose a framework for brand-aware redesign generation. Given a product name, the framework constructs a brand image survey report that summarizes product and market information, derives a creative direction from the report, and integrates this direction into a self-enhancement loop in which generated images are critiqued and prompts are revised. We evaluate the framework on 50 redesign tasks across five product categories, comparing it with Naive T2I, IP-Adapter/IT-Blender, and unconstrained self-enhancement under the same T2I backbone. By a VLM-as-Judge protocol to measure creativity and brand identifiability, the proposed framework achieves a more favorable trade-off between the two objectives, with particularly clear gains in highly constrained categories such as automotive and motorcycle, where the plausible design space is relatively limited compared with that of other product categories. These results suggest that dynamically eliciting and textualizing brand image can guide creative product design generation under brand image constraints.

title: Towards Seconds-level Video Representation: Quadratically Gated Feature Grid with Adaptive, Prediction-free Sampling
comment: 13 pages, 11 figures, 4 tables. Code available at https://github.com/MillenRosen/Q-GAS
summary: Implicit neural video representations are notoriously slow to build, which does not cross the basic practical threshold for most industrial applications. Here, we present Q-GAS, a coordinate-queryable video representation that couples multi-resolution explicit 3D feature grids with a compact SwiGLU-style quadratic-gating (QG) decoder and an error-aware, prediction-free sampler. The explicit grids avoid hash-collision coefficient sharing at the cost of modestly higher storage yet greatly boost the expressive capacity; the QG decoder introduces low-rank local second-order interactions to improve the nonlinear feature response. During fitting, a global error map periodically refreshes a high-error pool, and each batch mixes pool samples with uniform samples, which is free from the auxiliary model to predict difficult samples, thereby further escalating the efficiency. On UVG Beauty/Bosphorus/Jockey, Q-GAS fits and quantizes under 50 s on one RTX PRO 6000, decodes at over 370 FPS with mixed precision and about 146 FPS in FP32. In our PyTorch implementation, Q-GAS trains and quantizes 5.5-7.2 times faster than the evaluated Instant-NGP baseline and 19-28 times faster than RNeRV. Under a 90 s budget, it improves PSNR/MS-SSIM/LPIPS over the evaluated NeRV-family pipelines at comparable BPP over the measured overlap. We have shared our code at https://github.com/MillenRosen/Q-GAS for readers' free use.

title: Can Large Language Models Optimize Pretrained Neural Network Weights? A Multi-Phase Empirical Evaluation of Gradient-Free Editing in YOLO26 Object Detection
summary: Direct weight editing offers a gradient-free alternative to fine-tuning pretrained detectors, but its generalization and the value of large language model (LLM) guidance remain uncertain. We evaluate five experimental phases using YOLO26 models and MS COCO, comparing deterministic scaling, random perturbations, differential evolution, CMA-ES, structured interventions, real local-LLM proposals, failure-aware guidance, and hybrid LLM-CMA-ES against a matched random-policy control. Optimization uses native Ultralytics mAP50-95 on 1,000 COCO Val2017 images; selected candidates are assessed on a disjoint, previously examined 1,500-image subset, with COCO API AP50-95 reported separately where available. Increasing the CMA-ES budget from 8 to 250 evaluations raised development gains from +0.11 to +0.28 percentage points, while selection changes remained negative (-0.03 to -0.12 points); the 250-evaluation result uses one seed. The hybrid LLM approach showed no statistically established advantage over random-policy guidance (p = 0.612, 0.369, and 0.694 at budgets 8, 25, and 50). Five-seed YOLO26m replication yielded a COCO API AP difference of +0.004 points (95% CI: -0.026 to +0.034). Of 225 archived LLM proposals, 53 satisfy the final strict schema; early tensor-level execution cannot be fully verified. Genuine LLM-mediated weight editing is feasible, but the tested approaches did not demonstrate consistent transfer beyond the development subset or a measurable LLM advantage.

title: SceneAgent: A Multi-Agent Framework for Portable Game Scene Generation
summary: Moving a scene generator to a new game engine requires more than exporting its final output: planning, construction tools, and stored experience may also depend on the original backend. We present SceneAgent, a multi-agent framework for reusing the construction process and its experience across backends. A canonical SceneContext maintains the evolving world, while backend adapters isolate coordinate conventions, asset bindings, and export. Structured handoffs let fresh Builder sessions query this persistent state without inheriting the full construction transcript. Across generations, human-approved traces are distilled into asset-ID-free Layout skills and semantic Content skills that can be retrieved and recombined. We introduce GameSceneBench, comprising 69 indoor and outdoor prompts. Under a common asset and evaluation protocol, SceneAgent obtains human tie-adjusted preference scores of 78.2-89.4% against five baselines. Ablations show that reusable skills and the multi-agent protocol primarily improve prompt alignment and scene completeness, with additional runtime. Deployment in a second engine preserves the shared construction protocol and skill library while replacing backend integration components. Together, these results support separating persistent scene state, task-local reasoning, and reusable experience for portable scene construction.

title: V-JEPA-LM: Video-Language Models That Read Dynamics Beyond Static, Text-Aligned Representations
summary: World-model video encoders such as V-JEPA learn how scenes change (direction, speed, order, state) from video alone. To answer questions, they are joined to a language model trained on captions and question-answer pairs. But each caption or question names only a few attributes of a clip, so the model learns to retrieve those attributes rather than to read the clip, and the dynamics the encoder carries go unused: on the same items, a linear probe reads speed from frozen V-JEPA features at 87% while the VLM answers at chance. We show where dynamics lives in a frozen encoder: in a subspace shared across videos for predictive encoders such as V-JEPA, but not as a shared component of frame-wise, text-aligned encoders such as SigLIP. We then build counterfactual supervision that makes the language model read it: pixel transformations turn public videos into answer-balanced variants whose answers are set by the transformation and differ only in the change. Trained in a single stage on 4.53M public samples with 32 visual tokens per frame, where open video LLMs use several stages, 9M to 172M samples and 64 to 256 tokens per frame on average, the resulting V-JEPA-LM models (1B to 8B, Qwen3 and Llama) lead every size class in average score across eleven video benchmarks; our 4B model scores 72.1, against 61.1 for the best open 4B and 64.8 for the best open 8B model. A controlled encoder x supervision study shows that the encoder decides what can be read and the supervision what is read: at a matched budget, counterfactual supervision adds 4.5 points on average and 38 on the speed questions of natural benchmarks. Code and models: https://github.com/kkt94/Llama-V-JEPA-LM.

title: DySENSE: Dynamic Spatiotemporal ENergy Synthesis and Emulation with Satellite Imagery
summary: Cities account for over two-thirds of the world's energy and more than 70% of global carbon dioxide emissions. City energy is essential for achieving the 2050 net-zero target and the UN's Sustainable Development Goals 7 and 11. Although existing studies have made progress, they are limited by data and methodological gaps. Existing studies are largely predictive for existing cities rather than generative for future cities; fine-grained, aligned monthly dynamic energy data are scarce; and existing GenAI models struggle to generate dynamic urban functional monthly energy. We present DySENSE, a joint multimodal GenAI framework that synthesizes static urban satellite imagery together with spatially aligned, dynamic monthly building energy consumption maps. We decouple long-term static urban morphology from short-term dynamic energy consumption. By conditioning on static urban land use, DySENSE can generate realistic, diverse and new static urban imagery with aligned energy maps. By conditioning on dynamic monthly and climate prompts, DySENSE can jointly generate dynamic, monthly energy consumption maps while keeping the urban morphology static. Experiments across four cities (New York, Washington, Norfolk, Busan) demonstrated that DySENSE can generate annotated high-fidelity synthetic energy data using less than 25% labelled data, boosting downstream prediction performance by 8% mIoU, and achieving strong energy dynamic consistency. Compared to existing methods, DySENSE significantly improved prediction performance (8.7% accuracy) and reduced prediction error (9%-18% CVRMSE, ASHRAE). DySENSE offers an effective foundation for energy-efficient cities, peak-load analysis, building performance simulation and dynamic demand response for city, energy, and building science. The data and code: https://huggingface.co/datasets/skl24/MUSE2 and https://github.com/kailaisun/DySENSE

title: Photogrammetric 3D Model-Based Animal Behavior Classification
summary: Video-based behavior estimation is often implemented end-to-end from image sequences. We advocate a two-stage alternative: reconstruct 3D body and object geometry before classifying behavior. This makes ambiguities of the ill-posed 2D-to-3D inverse problem explicit and potentially correctable. We demonstrate the strategy with simulated interacting mice and extend it to real video.

title: More Genes, Faster Inference: Efficient Large-Panel Spatial Transcriptomics Prediction from Histology
summary: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) prediction from histology aims to infer spatially resolved gene expression profiles directly from tissue images. This is a challenging problem that is currently often addressed with complicated model architectures, additional inputs, and complicated training procedures, while remaining limited to fixed, small gene panels. This raises a natural question: Is there an efficient method for large-panel ST prediction? Here, we present GeneFlow, a simpler yet effective framework for large-scale spatial gene expression prediction that unifies flow-matching generative modeling with structured multimodal fusion. Specifically, GeneFlow first encodes both histological morphology and cross-gene interactions in spatial spots through histology and gene tokenizers. The model directly predicts spatial gene expression, rather than an intermediate velocity field, while being trained with a velocity-based flow-matching objective. We show that, even without relying on heavy generative pipelines, GeneFlow achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple ST benchmarks, with up to 56.8% gains in 1,000-gene prediction. Extensive experiments further show that GeneFlow produces biologically meaningful spot profiles while reducing computational cost by orders of magnitude, thereby improving efficiency and scalability, particularly in clinical settings. We believe GeneFlow provides an opportunity for leveraging widely available histology images for downstream biological discovery. Code is available at: https://github.com/ZZhangsm/GeneFlow

title: From Images to Grounded Edits: A Real-World Benchmark for Chinese Grammatical Error Correction in Handwritten Essays
summary: Chinese Grammatical Error Correction (CGEC) is typically formulated as a text-to-text problem. While suitable for digital texts, this formulation falls short in real-world K-12 education, where AI-assisted corrections are expected directly on essay images, which are primarily handwritten and exhibit many irregularities. To bridge this gap, we introduce Grounded Chinese Grammatical Error Correction (G-CGEC), an image-to-grounded-edit task requiring systems to predict both corrections and their positions on essay images. We propose G-CGEC-Eval, a benchmark comprising real-world images of K-12 Chinese essays with fine-grained annotations. For evaluation, we adapt IoU-based metrics from object detection and propose a more tolerant alternative based on center-distance matching. Using this benchmark, we evaluate open-source and proprietary vision-language models under a direct single-pass setting, as well as settings with auxiliary components (OCR and character grounding) coordinated via pipelining or agentic harnessing. Results show that even top-tier proprietary models perform surprisingly poorly in the single-pass setting, while pipelining and agentic harnessing yield meaningful improvements. Notably, an error-type-based multi-agent workflow achieves the best performance, establishing it as the strongest baseline for future G-CGEC research. Through ablations and fine-grained analysis, we find the task remains far from solved, with linguistic error discovery and character-level grounding as the primary bottlenecks. This underscores the need for models that better integrate visual perception with linguistic reasoning and visual grounding.

title: TelePhysica: Agentic Reconstruction of Physically Interactive Scenes
summary: Direct image-to-video diffusion models entangle pixel synthesis with implicit latent motion, precluding persistent 3D mechanical equilibrium, mid-rollout intervention, and counterfactual force control. Conversely, single-pass programmatic 3D reconstruction from an uncalibrated photograph leaves monocular depth and support clearance underconstrained, causing reconstructed scenes to interpenetrate or collapse under gravity. We present TelePhysica, a closed-loop framework that reconstructs an executable, multi-regime physical world from a single photograph to drive stateful 3D interaction and trajectory-grounded video synthesis. A vision-language coding agent synthesizes separable visual meshes and declarative physical models within a two-stage verification loop that pairs pixel-aligned silhouette critique with a zero-force gravitational equilibrium preflight. The verified world compiles into a unified solver coupling rigid bodies, articulated chains, co-dimensional cloth shells, and 3D tetrahedral elastodynamics, whose simulated rollouts condition pretrained video diffusion models through pixel-aligned structural streams. On a 100-scene single-image benchmark, closed-loop execution raises equilibrium-verified world recovery from $0\%$ in single-pass synthesis to $81\%$. Controlled constitutive ablations show over an order-of-magnitude larger localized corner displacement and out-of-plane pleating in finite-element cloth than in matched rigid-plate proxies. Conditioning video diffusion on simulated trajectories increases dynamic motion-mask overlap by $2{\times}\text{--}5{\times}$ and preserves motion direction under counterfactual force reversals where direct image-to-video models fail.

title: AG-JEPA: Anatomically Guided Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture for Neurodegenerative Representation Learning
summary: Brain MRI can reveal early signs of Alzheimers disease (AD) before measurable cognitive decline becomes apparent. However, during the transition from cognitively normal (CN) to mild cognitive impairment (MCI), the disease-related signals are often subtle and confined to only a few brain regions. Existing Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) models learn general structural representations but do not explicitly capture the anatomical regions affected in AD. We propose Anatomically Guided JEPA (AG-JEPA), which introduces anatomical tokens that interact with patch tokens during pretraining to learn region-specific representations from brain regions relevant to neurodegeneration. Building on this representation space, we further propose Prog-AG-JEPA, which models disease progression trajectory as a conditioned latent displacement within this space. We evaluate AG-JEPA across five downstream tasks spanning Alzheimer's disease diagnosis and progression prediction. AG-JEPA improves diagnosis and MCI prognosis, achieving an 8.4 percentage point AUROC gain over the strongest baseline on CN/MCI classification and a 7.1 percentage point gain on out-of-distribution CN/AD classification on the MR-RATE dataset, highlighting its effectiveness across both early-stage detection and cross-cohort generalization. For disease progression modeling, Prog-AG-JEPA consistently outperforms all baselines on future diagnosis and brain volume change prediction, demonstrating the value of anatomically grounded neurodegeneration representations for diagnosis and prognosis.

title: EcoVGGT: Pinned-Key Inference for Efficient and Streamable Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction from Long Videos
summary: Feed-forward multi-view transformers such as VGGT recover the cameras and geometry of a video in one pass, but the cost of their cross-frame attention grows quadratically with the frame count, and their accuracy drops on long videos. Most remedies approximate attention over all frames within a budget or select a few keys by their content. We hypothesize that the keys of a long video can be chosen without looking at its content, and our experiments on VGGT and $π^3$ support it: a few dozen evenly spread frames can serve as the keys of every frame. We present EcoVGGT, a training-free inference framework whose keys form a Pinned Key Set of 31 such frames. A pin pass stores their tokens in a Scene Cache, and the other frames read it in independent batches that reproduce joint inference with these keys exactly, at a constant cost per frame. An Online Stream updates the pinned frames during recording. Six middle global blocks align the frames and form a reusable VGGT module: the Alignment Score reads their attention to flag failures, and Alignment Refocusing reduces them by fine-tuning only these blocks (3.6 GPU hours). EcoVGGT ($π^3$) matches the success rate of $π^3$ on 1,000-frame ScanNet videos at 13.8 times its speed. With refocusing, EcoVGGT (VGGT) raises the success rate of VGGT from 70% to 82% at 8.5 times its speed on 500 frames. EcoVGGT reconstructs 4,000 frames on one GPU, and EcoVGGT ($π^3$) streams 1,000 frames at 18.6 frames per second with the lowest online absolute trajectory error.

title: AI-Based Multi-View Echocardiographic Image Synthesis using Dynamic Shape Control
comment: 5 pages, 2 figures, accepted for publication in the Proceedings of the 2026 IEEE International Ultrasonics Symposium (IUS 2026)
summary: Although automated methods have improved echocardiographic workflows, progress remains constrained by the need for large, well-annotated datasets. As the development of clinical databases is often limited by ethical and logistical challenges, synthetic data generation has emerged as a promising alternative. However, existing approaches commonly rely on left ventricle shape-based supervision or are tailored to specific cardiac views, limiting the generation of additional standard and unconventional imaging planes and the preservation of multi-view consistency across cardiac chambers. To address these limitations, we propose a novel framework for shape-controlled synthesis of multi-view echocardiographic sequences. First, multi-view cross-sections are extracted from dynamic whole-heart meshes. Ultrasound-like appearance is then introduced through a two-stage AI-based pipeline. In Stage 1, an unpaired GAN-diffusion model translates these cross-sections into realistic echocardiographic frames. As this translation is performed independently at the frame level, Stage 2 employs masked video reconstruction to improve temporal coherence and cardiac motion. Evaluation demonstrated high frame-level realism for both stages, while the integration of Stage 2 substantially improved video-level motion quality and temporal consistency. Overall, the proposed framework enables the generation of realistic multi-view echocardiographic sequences from diverse cardiac models, providing a scalable source of annotated data for dataset augmentation and the development of multi-view cardiac assessment methods.

title: CoPre-MoE: Consolidating and Preserving MoE for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning
summary: Multimodal continual instruction tuning requires multimodal large language models to sequentially acquire new capabilities without catastrophic forgetting. Mixture-of-experts (MoE) architectures offer a promising way to mitigate task interference through expert specialization and combination. However, while existing MoE-based methods avoid overwriting shared parameters by allocating separate experts for each task, this progressive expansion incurs severe cross-task redundancy and linear parameter growth. Specifically, experts across tasks often learn overlapping functions alongside task-specific capabilities. For instance, ScienceQA and TextVQA both locate relevant image regions. To curb parameter redundancy without inducing forgetting, we propose Consolidating and Preserving MoE (CoPre-MoE). For each incoming task, CoPre-MoE first learns task-specific MoE to capture specialized capabilities. To eliminate redundancy and reduce parameter growth across tasks, we design a shared-and-private expert architecture. Specifically, we first evaluate functional overlap to selectively consolidate overlapping experts across tasks into a fixed-capacity generic expert pool. We then factorize the remaining task-specific experts into shared projection bases and compact task-specific cores within a private expert pool. To mitigate forgetting, we construct the router by pairing each expert with learnable retrieval keys, where historical keys remain frozen during continual updates while newly added keys are regularized with an orthogonality penalty. At inference, input-dependent routing dynamically combines both pools without test-time task labels. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CoPre-MoE achieves superior performance while substantially reducing parameter overhead.

title: Monitoring peatland dynamics in the Baltic region using EGMS products
summary: Climate change and the increasing regulatory requirements to preserve natural carbon sinks have intensified interest in the large-scale monitoring of peatland ecosystems, which are among the most effective terrestrial environments for long-term carbon storage and hydrological regulation. In this context, Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) provides an opportunity to investigate peatland dynamics over extensive areas that are difficult to survey systematically on the ground, through repeated and cost-effective observations. This study tests the transferability of an open-source and reproducible methodology for the identification and monitoring of Peat-like Behaviour Areas (PBAs), based on Advanced Differential Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (A-DInSAR) time series provided by the European Ground Motion Service (EGMS), under the demanding observational conditions of the Boreal region, where snow cover, freeze–thaw processes and coherence loss produce sparse and discontinuous displacement series. The workflow combines Principal Component Analysis (PCA), K-means clustering and Density-Based Spatial Clustering (DBSCAN) to identify coherent areas characterised by peat-like displacement patterns and to distinguish sectors affected by subsidence from those exhibiting uplift behaviour. Applied across the Baltic countries within the Boreal biogeographical region, the methodology identified 576 PBAs (424 in Estonia, 125 in Latvia and 27 in Lithuania). A comparison with the CORINE Land Cover 2018 (CLC) inventory showed that approximately 43% of the identified PBAs occurred outside existing peatland inventories, highlighting the potential of the approach to identify areas exhibiting peat-like displacement patterns. Validation based on Sentinel-2 Total Productivity and Sentinel-3 OLCI Terrestrial Chlorophyll Index products revealed a strong spatial correspondence between the detected PBAs and areas characterised by reduced vegetation productivity and chlorophyll content. By distinguishing peatland sectors that are subsiding from those that are stable or rising, the approach provides a spatially continuous indicator of ecohydrological condition that complements static inventories, enabling degradation to be located within individual peatland systems and supporting the targeting and subsequent assessment of restoration interventions across different biogeographical regions.

title: Evaluation of Four Satellite-Derived High-Resolution Operational Sea Ice Concentration Products for Determination of Marginal Ice Zones Around Svalbard
summary: Marginal ice zone (MIZ) is a transitional region between dense pack ice and open water. It is a highly dynamic zone under strong interactions among the atmosphere, ocean, sea ice and waves, playing a crucial role in the polar climate system and ecosystem. Accurate determination of MIZ is, therefore, essential for advancing our understanding, modeling and prediction of the polar climate system and ecosystem. In this paper, we introduce and apply a comprehensive suite of MIZ-related metrics to evaluate the performance of four satellite-derived high-resolution operational sea ice concentration (SIC) products in characterizing the MIZs around Svalbard, using the Norwegian ice chart as reference. The metrics used for evaluation include sea ice extent (SIE), MIZ extent (MIZE), MIZ position, MIZ width, length of ice edge (LIE), integrated ice edge error (IIEE), integrated MIZ error (IME), ice edge distance error (IEDE), and MIZ width error (MWE). The evaluation is based on two years of daily SIC data (2024–2025) from four products, including the Bremen AMSR2 SIC data from the University of Bremen (Bremen SIC), the resolution-enhanced AMSR2 SIC (RE SIC) and Multisensor SIC products (Multisensor SIC) from the Norwegian Meteorological Institute, and the Automated Sea Ice Product (ASIP) from the Copernicus Marine Environment and Monitoring Service (CMEMS) (ASIP SIC). To be consistent with the Norwegian ice chart, the MIZ is defined as MIZ70 and MIZ90, corresponding to SIC thresholds of up to 0.7 and 0.9, respectively. The evaluation results demonstrate that all four satellite SIC products generally capture the evolution of the sea ice conditions around Svalbard well, but differ in their accuracies in characterizng the sea ice edge and MIZs. On the whole, the ASIP product agrees best with the ice chart in describing the sea ice edge and MIZ70 through a large number of metrics, in particular the primary metrics IIEE and IME70. The Bremen SIC product tends to overlook areas with low SIC, leading to a significant underestimate of SIE and a large IIEE. However, it provides an overall close agreement with the ice chart in the MIZE90. The RE SIC product exhibits good performance in capturing the SIE, but tends to notably overestimate the MIZE. Multisensor provides the closest agreement with the ice chart for the IME90, MWE90 and MWEa70, and ranks as the second-best product for the IIEE, IME70 and MWEr70. Our results suggest that SAR and low-frequency AMSR2 channels are especially effective for determining the lower bound of the MIZ, while high-frequency AMSR2 channels are more suitable for detecting the upper bound. In addition, the complex summer surface conditions pose significant challenges for satellite sensors in determining the ice edge and MIZ, resulting in large IEDE and MWE during this period. The results highlight both the capabilities and limitations of satellite-based data in characterizing the MIZ, particularly under the challenging summer conditions. Accurate delineation of MIZs may require significant advancements in satellite observation technologies, retrieval algorithms, and more robust methods for integrating multiple sources.

title: STAH-Net: A Spatio-Temporal Attention Hybrid Network for Coastal Wetland Vegetation Classification Using Multi-Source Sentinel-1/2 Time Series
summary: Accurate mapping of coastal wetland vegetation is essential for ecological conservation and blue carbon assessment, yet it remains challenging due to fragmented boundaries, spectral similarity among species, pronounced phenological variability, and limited generalization under small-sample conditions. We propose a spatio-temporal attention hybrid network (STAH-Net) for multi-source time-series classification. A 29-band feature cube is constructed from Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 data, integrating monthly Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) and vertical–vertical (VV) polarization time series with static spectral and polarimetric indices. An improved U-Net backbone with dual-branch 3D convolutions extracts optical and Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) temporal features in parallel, incorporating a Temporal Enhancement Attention Module (TEAM) for phenological weighting, a Local Channel Attention (LCA) module for channel recalibration, and Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling (ASPP) for multi-scale context. An edge-weighted hybrid loss combining edge-weighted cross-entropy and Dice loss mitigates class imbalance and boundary blurring. Experiments in Hangzhou Bay, Liaohe Estuary, and Minjiang Estuary achieves overall accuracy (OA) values of 98.16%, 97.23%, and 95.76%, respectively, with a maximum Kappa of 97.49%, outperforming ConvLSTM, U-Net, SegFormer, SITSMamba, and GLMambaNet under identical settings. Ablation and visual analyses confirm the effectiveness of the proposed modules, with NDVI phenology providing primary discrimination and VV offering complementary structural information. Cross-year and cross-region tests show promising transferability, with OAs of 97.21% and 94.75% in Liaohe Estuary for 2024 and 2020, respectively, and 93.83% in Shanghai. These results demonstrate that STAH-Net provides an effective and transferable workflow for coastal wetland vegetation mapping.

title: Cross-Sensor Characterization of the 26 August 2026 Nepal High-Mountain Hazard Cascade Using Landsat and Sentinel-1
summary: On 26 August 2026, a mass-movement and flood cascade affected the Nepal–China border region and propagated downstream through the Lende Khola–Trishuli river system. Rapid characterization of such high-mountain events is challenging because optical observations may be limited by cloud cover, while synthetic aperture radar (SAR) amplitude changes can reflect multiple surface and geometric effects. This study combined pre- and post-event Landsat 8/9 imagery with multi-temporal Sentinel-1 VV observations to determine whether the 2026 disturbance produced a spatially coherent radar response. A 5.52 km2 affected-area footprint was independently delineated from Landsat imagery and used to compare Sentinel-1 changes inside and outside the mapped disturbance along a 14.4 km valley corridor. A spatially matched 2025 sequence, which included a documented GLOF, was used to characterize spatial variability during a separate observation period. Within the mapped footprint, median absolute VV change during the 2026 event was 2.19 dB, compared with 1.66 dB outside, while median event anomaly was 0.56 and 0.06 dB, respectively. The inside–outside anomaly contrast was positive in 27 of 29 profile segments. After adjustment for the corresponding 2025 spatial contrast, the reference-adjusted spatial contrast remained positive in 25 of 29 segments, with a median of 0.344 dB. Direct recomputation of SAR pixel statistics over a common 14 km profile yielded positive reference-adjusted spatial contrasts in 85.7%, 92.9%, and 85.7% of units at 500 m, 1 km, and 2 km scales, respectively. The results indicate that the optically mapped 2026 disturbance coincided with a predominantly positive Sentinel-1 spatial contrast across the examined scales, although its magnitude and spatial prevalence depended partly on the aggregation procedure. A supplementary cross-orbit analysis showed positive inside–outside anomaly contrasts in both ascending (0.499 dB) and descending (0.251 dB) Sentinel-1 observations over common valid-pixel coverage. However, the descending acquisitions jointly covered only 59.9% of the Landsat-mapped footprint, limiting the spatial representativeness of this comparison. The proposed cross-sensor framework provides a simple approach for rapid characterization of high-mountain cascading hazards without interpreting SAR amplitude change as a direct event inventory.

title: An Object-Level Active Semantic-Driven Posterior Probability Change Detection Method for Remote Sensing Images with Limited Annotations
summary: Change detection in high-resolution remote sensing imagery is susceptible to the adverse effects of within-class spectral heterogeneity, shadows, and complex spatial structures. Meanwhile, change detection methods based on land-cover posterior probabilities generally rely on reliable semantic training information, making complete manual interpretation costly. To address these issues, this study develops a change detection framework that integrates SEEDS-guided SAM object construction and active learning-based interpretation with FCM-CSBN-CVAPS posterior probability inference. First, representative points of SEEDS superpixels are used as prompts for SAM to generate candidate objects and construct a mutually exclusive object partition. Second, based on the spectral statistical features of the superpixels and an XGBoost classifier, active learning is employed to select highly uncertain samples for limited manual annotation, thereby obtaining object-level semantic information. Finally, FCM is used to characterize pixel-level spectral uncertainty, while CSBN incorporates spatial context to estimate posterior probabilities of land-cover classes. Bi-temporal change measurement and changed-area extraction are then performed in the posterior probability space. Experimental results show that the proposed framework achieves stable change detection performance by manually annotating only approximately 10% of the superpixels in the target scenes. On DS1, DS2, and DS3, the Kappa coefficients reach 83.87%, 86.05%, and 90.21%, respectively, while the corresponding F1 scores are 87.62%, 91.78%, and 91.31%, achieving the highest Kappa and F1 scores among the evaluated methods under the specified experimental settings. These results indicate an effective balance between false-alarm suppression and missed-detection control for change detection using limited target-scene semantic annotations. In adaptive evaluation experiments, the mean Kappa and F1 scores reach 84.58% and 87.84%, respectively, further confirming the effectiveness and stability of the proposed framework across diverse remote sensing scenarios.

title: From Site-Level Detections to Monthly and Annual National Totals: Multiyear VIIRS Nightfire Estimates of Global Gas Flaring
summary: This study advances global gas-flaring monitoring from a sequence of annual inventories to a monthly, source-resolved, multi-satellite record of upstream gas flaring from March 2012 through December 2025, using VIIRS Nightfire observations from SNPP, NOAA-20, and NOAA-21. The analysis integrates a persistent multiyear flare catalog, a calibration derived from controlled flare tests relating radiant heat to gas flow rate, and an aggregation framework that separates clear non-detections from cloud-affected, sunlit, or otherwise invalid observations. The framework yields consistent monthly and annual estimates from individual flare sites to country and global scales. Global upstream flaring reached 164.5 BCM in 2025, the third consecutive annual increase, and was highly concentrated: 4.3% of active sites accounted for 80% of the global volume. Summed monthly estimates are internally consistent with direct annual estimates (median ratio 98.1%) while revealing seasonal patterns and short-term changes hidden in annual inventories. Global estimates from the three VIIRS instruments agree within 1–4%, and comparisons with regulatory records for Texas (Permian and Eagle Ford) and New Mexico, regions with reliable reporting but atypically small and intermittent flares, show strong temporal agreement (monthly r = 0.85–0.91) and recovery of 69–93% of reported volumes. Comparisons with legacy estimates further show that differences among flaring products reflect combined changes in source coverage, calibration, satellite sampling, and aggregation rather than a uniform rescaling of annual totals. Cloud-covered overpasses must be excluded rather than counted as non-detections, which would lower global volumes by 27–30%, and the catalog must be refreshed every 6–12 months to remain representative.

title: HiMambaMap: A Hilbert-Scanning Mamba Diffusion Network for Online Map Generation from Remote Sensing Imagery
summary: Remote sensing image-to-online map translation (RSMT) represents a critical research frontier in geographic information processing. With the rapid development of deep learning, generative models have attracted increasing attention for automatic map generation. However, existing methods incur substantial computational overhead when modeling global contextual information. Recently, Mamba has been widely adopted in remote sensing for capturing global dependencies with linear complexity. However, naively applying its sequential scanning mechanism to RSMT tends to disrupt local spatial relationships essential to map generation. In this study, we propose HiMambaMap, a Hilbert-scanning Mamba diffusion network for RSMT. Specifically, it is built upon a Brownian bridge diffusion model, where the proposed denoiser combines a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) encoder for local spatial feature extraction and a Mamba decoder for efficient global dependency modeling. To further improve the spatial consistency of the generated maps, we introduce a Multi-Scale Feature Fusion (MSFF) module into the denoiser for enhanced multi-scale feature fusion and incorporate a four-directional Hilbert scanning strategy into the Mamba decoder to better preserve spatial locality. Extensive experiments on two widely used datasets demonstrate that HiMambaMap achieves competitive generation quality and pixel-level color consistency, while maintaining the lowest parameter count and computational complexity among several state-of-the-art methods.

title: Dominant Factor in the Relationship Between Ice Thickness and Flow Velocity in the Downstream Region of Shirase Glacier, East Antarctica, Derived from Remotely Sensed Data
summary: The buttressing effect of landfast sea ice is crucial for the stability of Antarctic outlet glaciers. This study investigated spatiotemporal variations in flow velocity and ice thickness at the Shirase Glacier, East Antarctica, from 2016 to 2025 using ALOS-2/PALSAR-2 and CryoSat-2/SIRAL data. Flow velocity increased, and ice thickness decreased downstream, exhibiting a significant negative correlation (r = −0.66, p < 0.05). Notably, during periods of unstable landfast ice (2017–2018 and 2023–2025), substantial ice flow acceleration occurred in the downstream ice tongue. Furthermore, basal melt rates calculated using the Eulerian flux divergence method revealed high melting (16–20 m a−1) near the grounding line, decreasing to 2–4 m a−1 mid-stream, and increasing to 4–8 m a−1 near the ice front. This distribution is consistent with the subglacial oceanic vertical thermal structure. These results quantitatively demonstrate the significant control of both landfast ice stability and subglacial ocean circulation on the spatiotemporal dynamics of the Shirase Glacier.

title: SSC-DETR: Real-Time End-to-End Small-Object Detection in UAV Remote Sensing Imagery via Saliency-Guided Sparse Attention and Signed Sparse Semantic Calibration
summary: Small-object detection in UAV imagery is difficult because targets occupy only a few pixels amid cluttered backgrounds. Although high-resolution features preserve fragile spatial cues, dense contextual interaction over these features is computationally expensive, while multiscale fusion can weaken or misalign local semantic responses. We propose SSC-DETR, a real-time end-to-end detector that addresses these challenges through selective contextual interaction before fusion and selective semantic calibration afterward. Saliency-Guided Sparse Attention (SGSA) learns a spatial selection prior—a saliency map explicitly supervised by Gaussian targets derived from ground-truth bounding boxes—and uses it to select object-relevant high-resolution tokens for sparse self-attention while retaining dense local features elsewhere. Signed Sparse Semantic Calibration (SSSC) independently selects a smaller set of post-fusion positions and injects spatially aligned, bounded signed semantic residuals to reinforce useful evidence or suppress inconsistent responses. Haar-DWT downsampling and a scale-calibrated GIoU–GCD localization objective complement the two modules. Experiments on VisDrone and AI-TOD-v2 demonstrate improvements with ResNet-18 and ResNet-50. With ResNet-50, SSC-DETR increases AP from 29.6% to 35.2% on VisDrone and from 25.5% to 28.9% on AI-TOD-v2 while retaining real-time inference.

title: Focus, Magnify, and Detect: An Adaptive Region-Aware Detector for Remote Sensing Object Detection
summary: Object detection in remote sensing images (RSIs) suffers severely from small-scale instances, which are inherently constrained by extremely low pixel occupancy, fragile spatial detail retention, and insufficient discriminative feature representation. Global scaling is an intuitive strategy to compensate for the spatial information loss of small targets, yet it inevitably brings significant computational complexity as convolutional networks grow quadratically with the elevation of spatial resolution. In order to alleviate this accuracy–efficiency dilemma, we propose a focus, magnify, detect network, named adaptive region-aware detector (ARADet), tailored for object detection in RSIs. In the focus stage, our region-aware attention (RAA) module generates a Gaussian-constrained attention heatmap to rapidly localize potential small-target regions from the regional attention map. In the magnify stage, we introduce a differentiable affine magnification mechanism with learnable scaling factors. For each focused region, the network adaptively predicts a scaling factor and constructs a center-aligned affine transformation matrix to achieve center-preserving regional magnification. Unlike global upsampling schemes, our module only enhances target-region features and fills them back into the original feature map, thus keeping the overall feature resolution unchanged. The final enhanced features are fed into the detection head for category classification and oriented bounding-box regression. Extensive experiments conducted on two standard aerial object detection benchmarks, including DOTA and DIOR-R, demonstrate that ARADet brings 1.18% mAP improvement over the baseline method, with merely 0.3726M additional parameters. Although the introduced feature amplification yields a moderate rise in FLOPs, ARADet achieves favorable accuracy gains with negligible parameter overhead and surpasses many state-of-the-art oriented detectors.

title: Cross-Scene Transfer Accuracy of Geometric Correction Parameters for GF-3B/C SAR Imagery
summary: Accurate geometric positioning is essential for the quantitative application of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery. Although geometric calibration can effectively reduce systematic positioning errors, the cross-scene transferability of calibration-derived correction parameters remains insufficiently evaluated, particularly under different acquisition conditions. This study investigates the geometric positioning accuracy and parameter transferability of GF-3B/C SAR imagery using observations from the Xilinhot and Lijiang calibration sites. Scene-specific range and azimuth-time corrections were first estimated within the Range–Doppler framework, followed by cross-scene transfer experiments and acquisition-condition sensitivity analyses. The results indicate that scene-specific correction established a high-accuracy baseline, reducing the median planimetric root-mean-square error (RMSE) from 57.50 m to 1.53 m. In cross-scene transfer, the range correction exhibited substantially higher stability than the azimuth-time correction. Range-only transfer yielded a median combined two-dimensional RMSE of 50.98 m, whereas combined transfer yielded 60.51 m, compared with 57.85 m before transfer. Transfer performance was associated with source–target acquisition compatibility, yielding superior accuracy when satellite platform, orbit direction, and Doppler centroid frequency differences were well matched. Furthermore, cross-site transfer demonstrated accuracy comparable to that of same-site transfer under compatible conditions. These findings indicate that parameter transferability depends on both the specific correction component and acquisition compatibility. For GF-3B/C imagery in ground-control-point-free (GCP-free) scenarios, range corrections offer strong potential for direct reuse, whereas azimuth-time corrections require rigorous compatibility screening during source-scene selection.

title: A 1 km Surface Soil Moisture Product Downscaled from SMAP Using MODIS Shortwave-Infrared Reflectance for the Tibetan Plateau Validated Across Five In Situ Networks
summary: Surface soil moisture (SSM) regulates land–atmosphere water and energy exchanges over the Tibetan Plateau (TP); yet, passive microwave SSM products, such as those from the Soil Moisture Active Passive (SMAP) mission, are limited to coarse spatial resolutions of tens of kilometers. Although various downscaling approaches have been developed using radar backscatter, thermal infrared observations, and optical–thermal indicators, the value of shortwave infrared (SWIR) reflectance—whose moisture-dependent absorption characteristics offer fine-scale soil moisture information—remains insufficiently assessed across contrasting environments. To address this gap, we developed a 1 km SSM product for 2017–2020 by downscaling 36 km MCCA-SMAP estimates over the TP, combining the normalized shortwave difference soil moisture index (NSDSI) derived from MODIS reflectance with a first-order Taylor expansion and daily sensitivity calibration. The product was evaluated against ground observations from five monitoring networks spanning diverse climatic and land surface conditions using spatial, temporal, regional-scale, and spatiotemporal comparison frameworks, and was benchmarked against three published 1 km downscaled products based on radar backscatter, diurnal temperature amplitude, and soil evaporation efficiency, respectively. Compared with the original MCCA-SMAP SSM, the spatial regression slopes of the NSDSI-based downscaled product moved closer to unity at all five networks, with spatial correlations increasing at four networks particularly at SMN-WDL (from −0.04 to 0.59) and Shiquanhe (from 0.12 to 0.44), although the near-unity slopes at Shiquanhe were sensitive to unusually high estimates at SQ11. The NSDSI-based downscaled product showed lower mean station-level temporal correlations across the five networks, whereas regional-scale temporal correlations remained nearly unchanged. Relative to the existing 1 km products, the NSDSI-based product had spatial slopes closer to unity at all networks except Maqu, although correlation and error rankings varied among networks. At Maqu, where the vegetation cover is relatively high, the NSDSI-based downscaled SSM had spatial correlations below 0.2 and exhibited lower correlations and a higher ubRMSD than the radar- and thermal inertia-based downscaled products. The resulting downscaled SSM maps preserved the broad west-to-east moisture gradient and showed finer spatial detail. These multi-network results identify improved spatial pattern representation as the principal benefit of the evaluated SWIR-assisted downscaling approach, while demonstrating that gains in spatial agreement do not necessarily improve temporal performance or reduce ubRMSD.

title: Irrigation Channel Mapping from Very High-Resolution Satellite Imagery and LiDAR-Derived Digital Elevation Models
summary: Comprehensive spatial inventories of irrigation channels inform water-resource management, hydrological modeling, and infrastructure planning, yet remain unavailable for many irrigated regions due to the high cost of manual mapping. Here we present a novel approach for irrigation channel mapping that integrates very high-resolution (0.3–0.5 m) WorldView satellite imagery, 1 m LiDAR-derived digital elevation model data, and ancillary land cover and irrigation datasets. The approach employs a U-Net convolutional neural network and a Hessian filter to identify potential surface-water features from optical imagery, while geomorphon classification identifies potential channel locations from digital elevation model data. A constrained dilation algorithm expands high-confidence channel detections along topographically favorable paths, and an XGBoost classifier distinguishes irrigation channels from natural surface-water features and false positives. Applied to a 569 km2 study area in the San Luis Valley, Colorado, the approach mapped 552 linear kilometers of irrigation channels—18% more than the U.S. Geological Survey National Hydrography Dataset Plus High Resolution and 35% more than the Colorado Division of Water Resources inventory. Object-based accuracy assessment indicated that 92.3% of mapped channel segments were definite or possible irrigation channels, with only 7.7% representing false positives. Among channel segments not appearing in existing datasets, 76% were judged to be definite (43%) or possible (33%) irrigation channels either missed by previous mapping efforts or constructed after the creation of those datasets. While recall (the proportion of reference channel pixels that were correctly mapped) remained limited (0.28), the approach demonstrates potential for rapidly generating spatially explicit channel inventories that provide a starting point for manual refinement: false positives can be removed quickly, whereas adding missed channels requires more substantial effort.

title: VMCF: VMamba–CNN Fusion Network for Sea Surface Temperature Prediction
summary: Sea surface temperature (SST) exerts a critical influence on diverse physical and biological processes within the marine environment. Nevertheless, accurate short-term SST forecasting still remains challenging. Current deep learning (DL) models have two key limitations: first, the convolutional neural network (CNN)-based methods fail to capture global spatiotemporal dependencies; second, Transformer-based approaches suffer from relatively high computational costs. To address these issues, this study introduces a VMamba–CNN fusion network (VMCF), a dual-branch architecture designed to effectively characterize the multiscale temporal and spatial variability of SST. The VMCF combines the powerful local feature extraction capability of CNNs with the efficient linear-computability global spatiotemporal representation of VMamba, further strengthened via channel-wise feature fusion. Extensive experiments on the OISST dataset demonstrate significant performance improvements across all evaluation metrics, clearly validating the superiority of VMCF in SST forecasting. Specifically, it achieves root-mean-square error (RMSE) values ranging from 0.17 °C to 0.51 °C across 1–10-day lead times, outperforming five state-of-the-art DL models.

title: Mangrove Disturbance and Recovery Following Hurricanes Irma and Maria (2017) in Florida and Puerto Rico
summary: Two U.S. National Estuarine Research Reserves (NERRs), Rookery Bay (Florida) and Jobos Bay (Puerto Rico), experienced hurricanes in September 2017 (Irma and Maria) and 2022 (Ian and Fiona). We quantified mangrove canopy disturbance and recovery using pixel-wise annual land-cover trajectories from 2 m WorldView™ imagery (2017–2024) and monthly Sentinel-2 and Landsat Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) time series (2016–2025). Mangrove target areas (MTAs) comprised pixels classified as mangrove in the pre-storm 2017 map and consistent coverage across the subsequent available maps. In 2018, mapped mangrove cover declined to 47% in the southeastern Rookery Bay MTA (sRB-MTA) and 59% in the Jobos Bay MTA (JB-MTA), with most disturbed pixels reclassified as soil. Intermediate mapped classes represented spectral and surface-condition changes rather than discrete ecological states. Despite greater initial loss, mapped mangrove cover reached 90% in the sRB-MTA by 2023, compared with 79% in the JB-MTA in 2023 and 83% in 2024. Recovery was spatially heterogeneous: pixels initially reclassified as mixed low-relief vegetation showed higher recovery percentages by 2023 (sRB-MTA: 92%; JB-MTA: 81%) than those reclassified as coastal water (48% and 23%, respectively). Persistent non-recovery of mangrove class coincided with pre-existing hydrologic stressors in both regions, and unauthorized coastal development in Jobos Bay NERR. Areas that subsequently returned to the mangrove class showed a sharp post-storm NDVI decline, followed by an initial rapid rebound and gradual recovery toward climatological greenness and seasonality by mid-2022. NDVI recovery began earlier in Jobos Bay (November 2017) than in southern Rookery Bay (June 2018). No widespread canopy response was detected following the 2022 storms, consistent with weaker local wind exposure but not excluding other ecological effects. Together, land-cover trajectories and the NDVI resolved complementary canopy recovery patterns without establishing restoration of pre-storm forest structure or ecosystem function.

title: Identifying Focal Indicators for Localized SDG 14-Aligned Evaluation in China’s Coastal Provinces Through an Integrated Assessment Framework
summary: Identifying focal indicators is essential for improving localized SDG 14-aligned assessment amid diverse pressures and governance challenges in coastal areas. However, indicator-level diagnosis remains constrained by the lack of a coherent and unified assessment framework. Focusing on 11 coastal provinces of China, this study constructs a localized SDG 14-aligned indicator system based on the pressure-state-response (PSR) framework, evaluates indicators in terms of score, interaction, and network centrality, and integrates these components into a multi-criteria analysis (MCA) framework to identify focal indicators for coastal sustainable development. The results show that the share of tertiary marine industries is identified as a high-scoring positive-interaction central indicator, while fishing vessel tonnage per capacity unit is identified as a high-scoring trade-off-related central indicator. In addition, fishery economic output per GDP is identified as a low-scoring-trade-off-related central indicator. These findings suggest that future coastal development should place greater emphasis on marine industrial upgrading, fishing-capacity regulation, and the coordinated improvement of fishery economic benefits and sustainability performance, so as to create more favorable conditions for strengthening synergistic development. The proposed framework supports indicator-level diagnosis and differentiated management attention for localized coastal sustainable development.

title: Long-Term Trends and Interannual Coupling of Spring Green-Up Onset and Canopy Maturation in Northern China’s Forests
summary: The start of season (SOS) is widely used to assess forest phenological responses to climate change, but how well it represents subsequent canopy greening remains unclear. Using GIMMS NDVI3g and climate data for 1983–2014, we examined greenness-defined SOS and the start of canopy maturity (SOM) across deciduous needleleaf (DNF), mixed (MF), and deciduous broadleaf (DBF) forests in northern China, and assessed the additional explanatory information provided by seasonal climate beyond SOS. After detrending, SOS and SOM were positively correlated in all three forest types (r = 0.57–0.80, all p < 0.01). However, long-term trend estimates showed regional differences: SOS and SOM tended to advance in DNF and DBF, whereas SOS tended to advance and SOM to be delayed in MF. SOS alone accounted for 34.7–58.3% of the interannual variation in SOM; seasonal climate explained additional SOM variation in DBF after accounting for SOS. Thus, although spring green-up onset and later canopy greening are significantly correlated at the interannual scale, they do not necessarily follow parallel long-term trajectories. Incorporating both spring onset and subsequent canopy greening, together with their seasonal climate associations, into phenological models may improve projections of forest spring development under climate change.

title: Three-Dimensional GNSS Water Vapor Tomography for Object-Based Precipitation Precursor Identification in Complex Terrain
summary: Conventional water vapor–precipitation studies rely on column-integrated or single-site observations, which cannot capture the three-dimensional (3D) structure of moisture aggregation and its role in precipitation triggering in complex terrain where convective, frontal, and orographic rainfall coexist. Using Ningxia Continuously Operating Reference Station (NXCORS) Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) observations (2018–2021), we develop a 3D water vapor tomography model (5 km × 6 km × 1 km computational grid; 5 min retrieval interval), validated against independent radiosonde and ERA5 data (r = 0.953/0.881; RMSE = 1.998/1.949 g m−3). We propose 3D Water Vapor Preferential Zones (WVPZs) and an object-based framework using stratified dual-percentile thresholds (99%/97%) and 3D connected-component tracking to identify, track, and match WVPZs with rainfall regions under temporal (≤6 h prior) and spatial (≤100 km centroid distance) constraints. Across 16 events, WVPZs were present in 94.97% of 5 min time steps. In 416 matched pairs, WVPZs typically formed 2–6 h before rainfall, with a mean precursor time lag of 231.5 min at onset. Mean centroid distances were 52–55 km (mean minimum centroid distance: 39.4 km). By rainfall type, convective rainfall had the shortest precursor time lag (220.6 min) but largest distance (55.7 km); frontal rainfall showed the tightest coupling (49.1 km); orographic rainfall had the longest precursor time lag (254.0 min). Sample-derived precursor-lag and spatial-proximity ranges are 3–5 h and 30–60 km. This framework shifts moisture diagnosis from continuous fields to discrete, trackable water vapor objects, providing a quantitative 3D indicator for characterizing pre-precipitation moisture organization and supporting precipitation monitoring in complex terrain.

title: GACN: A Dual-Branch Graph Attention Convolutional Network for Cloud Detection Using Himawari-8/9 AHI
summary: Clouds are core components of the global climate system and hydrological cycle, and high-precision cloud detection is a key prerequisite for quantitative optical remote sensing applications. Traditional threshold methods often miss thin clouds and misclassify high-albedo surfaces; existing pixel-level models ignore spatial context, causing class imbalance and detection bias. This study proposes the graph attention convolutional network (GACN) for daytime and nighttime cloud detection across land cover types using Advanced Himawari Imager (AHI) data. It adopts a dual-branch architecture to extract spatial correlations and multi-scale spectral features, paired with an adaptive fusion gate and multi-objective joint loss to balance detection performance. The graph attention branch builds dynamic spatial–spectral neighbor graphs to resolve spectral confusion between thin clouds and bright underlying surfaces. The proposed metric-constrained joint loss is also portable to other network architectures to mitigate class imbalance in pixel-level remote sensing classification. Trained on 2 km Himawari-8/9 AHI data with CALIPSO lidar labels, GACN achieves a TSS of 75.18% (daytime) and 71.57% (nighttime) with DR below 7%, outperforming seven baselines and two official AHI cloud mask variants. It provides an effective solution for high-accuracy AHI cloud mask generation and is more suited for regional-scale applications or offline post hoc scientific processing.

title: MFM-TransUNet: Multi-Scale Feature Modeling Network for Remote Sensing-Based Surface Water Extraction
summary: Accurate extraction of surface water is of great significance for water resource management, ecological conservation, and flood disaster monitoring. However, water bodies in high-resolution remote sensing imagery are often obscured by building shadows, vegetation, complex backgrounds, or spectral confusion. Consequently, traditional semantic segmentation methods frequently struggle with global feature modeling and the preservation of boundary details. To address these challenges, this paper proposes MFM-TransUNet, a remote sensing water extraction network based on multi-scale feature modeling. The network employs an encoder–feature modeling–decoder architecture. A Ghost-SE encoder is utilized to extract multi-scale hierarchical features, while a High-Performance Sequence Modeling Module (HPSM) is introduced to aggregate local contextual information from high-level features through depthwise 1D convolutions, with a feed-forward network enhancing nonlinear feature representations along the channel dimension. During the decoding phase, a learnable weight-fusion strategy is applied to balance the contributions of features from different levels, and an Edge-enhanced Feature Attention (EFA) is incorporated to strengthen boundary-related information within the decoded features. The proposed method was evaluated in terms of segmentation accuracy, module ablation, and cross-dataset performance. Experiments on the GID dataset demonstrate that MFM-TransUNet achieves an Overall Accuracy (OA) of 96.27%, a Mean Intersection over Union (Mean IoU) of 89.24%, an F1-Score of 94.20%, and a Boundary IoU of 63.52%, showing competitive performance compared with several mainstream baseline models. Ablation studies evaluate the contributions of the key modules, while experiments on the LJ-Water and Water-CD datasets assess the model’s performance across different datasets. These results suggest that MFM-TransUNet achieves a favorable trade-off between segmentation accuracy, boundary-related performance, and computational cost, providing a potential approach for surface water extraction in complex remote sensing scenarios.

title: Combinatorial Selection of Multi-Pass ICESat-2 ATL24 Calibration Tracks for Sentinel-2 Satellite-Derived Bathymetry
summary: ICESat-2 ATL24 data provide along-track shallow-water depths that can serve as spaceborne calibration information for satellite-derived bathymetry (SDB). A study area is usually crossed by multiple passes, but the tracks differ in quality, depth coverage, and spatial coverage. Existing studies still mainly pool all tracks, use a single pass, or refine the data point by point, and no systematic method yet exists for selecting among large numbers of candidate-track combinations. We formulate ATL24 track selection as a combinatorial optimization problem whose objective is the bathymetric retrieval error, measured against independent airborne lidar bathymetry (ALB) reference depths within the study area so that selection requires local survey data, and test it in three coral-reef areas whose depth ranges and track-quality structures complement one another, using two retrieval models of different flexibility, XGBoost and the Stumpf band-ratio model. On a 16-track controlled pool small enough to enumerate, with the exhaustive global optimum as ground truth, a genetic algorithm (GA) reproduced the global optimum exactly in three of the six cases formed by the three study areas and two models and came within 1.28% of it in the other three, while evaluating fewer than 1% of all possible subsets; on randomly composed pools the GA approached the optimum equally reliably, whereas random search with the same number of evaluations found it with a probability below 1%. The GA was then extended to full candidate pools of 42–70 tracks, corresponding to 1012–1021 subsets, and compared with four conventional practices under spatial-block five-fold cross-validation. Relative to pooling all tracks, the root-mean-square error (RMSE) fell by 9.2–63.3% for XGBoost and by 2.2–30.5% for Stumpf (a magnitude sensitive to the Stumpf fitting settings), and all of these gains kept their sign under strict spatial isolation, in which the calibration points inside the test blocks were also withheld. The gains were concentrated in the deepest water, and some shallower depth bands deteriorated. These results show that the value of an ATL24 calibration track is determined jointly by track quality, coverage complementarity, and the downstream model, and that, where local reference depths are available, task-oriented combinatorial selection is better suited than the per-track thresholds and rankings tested here to the quality control of multi-pass calibration data.

title: Subpixel Low-Intensity Fire Detection in Wide-Swath Remote Sensing: Dual-Scale Thermal Background Adaptation and Spatiotemporal Semantic Constraints
summary: Subpixel low-intensity fires are difficult to detect in wide-swath imagery because mixed pixels weaken their thermal signals, whereas industrial facilities and photovoltaic panels can generate false alarms. We propose a dual-scale adaptive thermal background thresholding method based on spatiotemporal semantic constraints and conduct experiments using the detection of crop straw burning in China as a specific application scenario. The method combines scene-wide thermal state classification with local neighborhood statistics to adjust the above-background threshold and recover additional weak fire candidates. Farmland support, a persistent heat source prior derived from long-term VIIRS observations, and candidate-to-source proximity are then applied to newly added candidates to suppress non-target anomalies while preserving strong thermal detections. Experiments using 36 Wide Swath Imager scenes, near-contemporaneous Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite observations, field surveys in Anhui Province, and 260 Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer scenes support the method’s use for weak fire candidate screening under heterogeneous thermal backgrounds. Targeted field surveys found fresh crop residue burn marks at 10 of 12 selected T0 candidate sites (83.3%). This proportion applies only to the surveyed candidate set and does not represent an estimate of overall detection accuracy. In the MODIS transfer experiment, detections near industrial facilities decreased from 45.17% for the official products to 7.92% with the transferred method. The proposed framework supports the regional screening of low-intensity fire candidates and targeted field verification, with persistent heat source information providing contextual constraints.

title: HSFFNet: A Height-Guided Spatial–Frequency Fusion Network for Crown-Level Tree Species Segmentation
summary: High-resolution UAV RGB imagery and canopy height models (CHMs) can provide complementary appearance and structural information for tree crown analysis. However, existing multimodal segmentation methods often treat optical and height data as parallel feature sources, and the structural role of canopy height in tree crown representation remains insufficiently explored.
