To address this limitation, we propose HSFFNet, a Height-Guided Spatial–Frequency Fusion Network for crown-level tree species segmentation, which exploits CHM-derived structural information to enhance RGB representations across multiple feature scales and frequency components. Specifically, a Scale-Aligned Height Encoder (SAHE) is introduced to construct hierarchical height representations corresponding to the multilevel RGB features. A Height-Guided Spatial–Frequency Fusion (HGSFF) module then models appearance and structure interaction in the spatial domain while using canopy height to regulate frequency-specific RGB responses. Finally, a Multi-Scale Height-Frequency Refinement (MHFR) module is applied to extract localized height variations at multiple spatial ranges to complement structural details. Experiments on two tree species datasets show that HSFFNet achieves mIoU values of 78.26% and 79.05%, respectively, outperforming several representative RGB-based and multimodal segmentation methods.

title: Orientation-Aware Feature Flow Network for Oriented Object Detection in Remote Sensing Images
summary: Remote sensing oriented object detection faces the challenge of maintaining consistent rotational geometric information throughout feature representation, cross-scale propagation, and bounding-box localization. To address this issue, this paper proposes a direction–scale collaborative optimization method for oriented object detection. A frozen DINOv3 encoder is adopted as the semantic feature source to enhance target discrimination in complex backgrounds through global semantic modeling and dense feature representation. Rotation-Oriented Space-to-Depth Convolution (ROSPD) is introduced to preserve fine-grained spatial structures and local directional-response cues during downsampling. In addition, a Rotation-Aware Residual Fusion (RARF) module estimates local axial agreement between adjacent feature levels and uses it to condition residual multi-scale fusion. A ProbIoU–NWD joint loss with deterministic target-size-adaptive weighting is further constructed: it emphasizes NWD supervision for small objects and gradually returns to ProbIoU as target size increases, thereby improving localization stability under low-overlap conditions. Experiments on DIOR-R and DOTA-v1.5 demonstrate that the proposed method effectively improves the detection and localization performance of multi-scale oriented objects in complex remote sensing scenes.

title: Reconstruction of VIIRS 375 m Resolution Data for Algal Bloom Detection
summary: The Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS) is fundamentally constrained by a 750 m spatial resolution in its multispectral channels, limiting its capacity for algal bloom observations. This study proposed a Spatial Residual Correlation Method (SRCM) to reconstruct 375 m VIIRS ocean color products using the 375 m I1 band (638 nm). This method is based on the scale-invariance assumption that the linear relationships (k(λ)) between spatial residuals between M-bands and I1 band are almost identical at 375 m and 750 m, and calculates a scene-specific k(λ) to derive 375 m spatial residuals of M-bands from those of the I1 band. The reconstructed 375 m remote sensing reflectance (Rrs) and chlorophyll-a (Chl-a) images show additional spatial variation compared with the native 750 m products. The ratios of reconstructed to native products are 1.001 ± 0.029 for Rrs(443) and 0.997 ± 0.032 for Chl-a, indicating consistency with the native 750 m products. The 375 m ratio of algal bloom (RAB) maps show finer spatial patterns for reported algal bloom events in the tested coastal waters. These results suggest that SRCM may be useful for algal bloom detection in the tested coastal waters, while further comparisons with independent imagery at higher spatial resolution would allow the accuracy of the added features to be assessed.

title: A Spectral–Spatial Fusion Network for Hyperspectral Small Water Body Extraction
summary: In hyperspectral imagery, small water bodies are often difficult to delineate due to their limited spatial extent, irregular shapes, and spectral similarity to surrounding land-cover types, which can lead to missed detections and fragmented boundaries. To address these challenges, this study proposes a spectral–spatial fusion network with parallel 3D CNN and ResNet-50 branches to extract complementary spectral–spatial and hierarchical spatial features. A progressive gated spectral–spatial fusion (PGSSF) module integrates these features across successive scales to help preserve weak water-body features and reduce background interference. The fused features are further processed by a scale-adaptive local–global (SALG) module, which combines local spatial details with broader contextual information to better characterize narrow watercourses and their continuity. Experiments were conducted using hyperspectral imagery from the Dongting Lake region, with comparisons against the normalized difference water index (NDWI), U-Net, Swin Transformer, and WaterFormer. The proposed method achieved a Water IoU of 80.68%, a recall of 90.33%, and an F1-score of 89.31%, with Water IoU exceeding that of WaterFormer by 4.76 percentage points. These results demonstrate the potential of the proposed method for regional small-water-body mapping and surface-water monitoring.

title: DecoupledFM: Decoupling Invariant and Specific Representations for Robust Cross-Modal Feature Matching
summary: Cross-modal image matching, such as between optical-SAR or RGB-infrared images, remains a critical yet challenging task due to severe, non-linear radiometric distortions that plague existing end-to-end matchers. We identify feature entanglement as a potential cause of this performance degradation: standard backbones implicitly couple modality-invariant geometric structures with modality-specific appearances. This coupling, while effective within a single domain, breaks down under drastic domain shifts, leading to matching failure. To address this, we propose DecoupledFM, a semi-dense matching framework that uses separate invariant and specific feature branches. The core of our method is the Invariance-Guided Disentanglement Module (IGDM), which enforces a trio of synergistic constraints—feature cyclic substitution for modality invariance, reconstruction with an orthogonality loss for disentanglement completeness, and keypoint score prediction for geometric saliency awareness—to achieve a principled decomposition. This novel design effectively injects the structural priors of sparse descriptors into a high-precision semi-dense architecture. During inference, only the disentangled invariant features are used for robust coarse matching via an Efficient Cross-View Matching Module, while fine refinement also uses backbone features. Extensive experiments on 20 challenging subsets demonstrate that DecoupledFM achieves state-of-the-art performance, significantly outperforming existing methods.

title: Quality-Gated Integration of Predicted Fields for Maize–Soybean Mapping with AlphaEarth Foundations
summary: Timely field-level crop mapping remains difficult where current labels and reliable parcel boundaries are scarce. This study examined whether 2024 AlphaEarth Foundations (AEF) annual embeddings could support maize–soybean mapping through unsupervised clustering followed by label-assisted semantic assignment and whether Fields of the World (FTW) predictions could convert pixel clusters into reliable parcel-level maps. The 64-dimensional AEF features at 10 m resolution were clustered without crop labels in an agricultural region of northern Northeast China. After the cluster solution was fixed, the field observations were used for semantic assignment and spatially blocked assessment. At the 652 route-based reference points collected in this study, direct AEF clustering yielded F1-scores of 0.944 for maize and 0.942 for soybean, with a macro-F1 of 0.943 for binary maize–soybean retrieval. Unconditional parcel assignment increased spatial regularity but reduced agreement with the reference observations. A quality gate based on pixel support, within-field purity, and under-segmentation risk retained a macro-F1 of 0.936 while reducing small patches by 31.0%. Selective use of predicted fields reduced fragmentation while preserving most of the sample-based accuracy of direct AEF clustering, offering a way to control the loss of pixel-level crop information during parcel aggregation.

title: From Pixels to Piezometers: Bridging Satellite Gravimetry and Groundwater-Level Analysis to Estimate Aquifer Specific Yield
summary: Groundwater is a critical resource in arid and semi-arid environments, where it supports agriculture and ensures drinking water. However, in many regions, including Morocco, this resource is experiencing significant stress, urging the need to understand the aquifers’ behavior. In this context, providing estimates of specific yield (Sy) is essential. This study combines terrestrial water storage (TWS) from GRACE-SeDA (Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment Self-Supervised Data Assimilation), and the groundwater storage (GWS) residual obtained from it by subtracting modeled soil moisture, snow water equivalent, and reservoir storage, with groundwater levels. A detailed analysis of groundwater-level time series using Sen’s slope shows a general and systematic depletion in almost all of the piezometers, with level decline ranging from weak trends to strong declines above −0.14 m/month. Similarly, the cumulative monthly GWS from the median of the 25-member ensemble shows a decreasing trend with a Sen’s slope of −13.23 million cubic meters (MCM) per month. A robust Huber loss function is employed to optimize Sy by minimizing the residuals between derived GWS anomalies and changes inferred from groundwater-level observations. Sy estimates exhibit spatial variability across the aquifer, ranging from 0.59 to 3.49% for GWS-derived values. The specific yield estimates are drawn from a 15-member ensemble crossing three soil moisture and five snow water equivalent sources. The obtained results fall within the range of observed Sy values. Nevertheless, uncertainties in remote sensing retrievals, spatial resolution, and subsurface heterogeneity limit the robustness of the approach.

title: Joint Assimilation of FY-3E Microwave Sounding and Ground-Based Microwave Radiometer Observations Incorporating AI-Based Cloudy-Sky Profile Retrievals over Complex Terrain on the Eastern Margin of the Tibetan Plateau
summary: Forecasting convective precipitation over complex terrain requires accurate thermodynamic initialization. We developed a WRFDA 3D-Var framework combining nominally clear-sky FY-3E MWTS-3/MWHS-2 radiances, artificial-neural-network (ANN)-retrieved cloudy-sky thermodynamic profiles, and ground-based microwave radiometer (MWR) profiles. In a 5–15 July 2024 inner-domain sample, cloud routing assigned 66.1% of MWTS-3 and 66.9% of MWHS-2 fields of view to the cloudy-sky pathway. Independent radiosonde validation yielded RMSEs of 2.537 K for land temperature and 1.071 g kg−1 for bias-corrected land specific humidity, although a −1.748 K cold bias remained in temperature. Principal precipitation comparisons of four experiments (CTRL, FY, MWR, and FY-MWR) used a common CV7 background-error covariance configuration across nine daily forecasts over Chongqing during 7–15 July. During the principal 10–11 July event, MWR performed comparatively well at selected light-to-moderate precipitation thresholds, whereas FY-MWR had the highest TS at the highest 24 h thresholds. In pooled nine-day verification, CTRL retained the highest threat scores at 0.1–50 mm, while FY-MWR had the highest point estimate at 100 mm (0.083 versus 0.048 for CTRL); however, the paired bootstrap confidence interval for the FY-MWR-minus-CTRL difference included zero. Instability, convective inhibition, moisture-flux convergence, and vertical-motion diagnostics showed time-dependent relationships with precipitation differences. The results therefore indicate event- and intensity-dependent forecast responses rather than uniformly improved forecasts.

title: Climatic Controls of Interannual Variability in Forest Land Surface Phenology Across Poland
summary: Understanding how consistently forest phenology responds from year to year is important for characterizing vegetation responses to climatic variability, yet most studies have focused on long-term phenological trends. Here, we assessed the spatial patterns and environmental controls of detrended interannual variability in the start (SOS) and end (EOS) of the growing season across Polish forests during 2003–2025. SOS and EOS were derived from MODIS NDVI time series, while climatic controls were evaluated using variable-specific preseason windows. Generalized additive models were used to relate phenological variability to long-term climatic conditions, interannual climate variability, aridity, and topography. SOS and EOS variability showed distinct spatial patterns and contrasting climatic sensitivities. SOS was most strongly associated with temperature during the 30-day preseason, whereas EOS showed weaker and more variable climatic relationships. The relevant preseason periods differed among climatic variables and between SOS and EOS. Environmental relationships were predominantly nonlinear, with important effects of temperature, precipitation, soil moisture, solar radiation, aridity, and elevation. The models explained 35.2% and 51.6% of the deviance in SOS and EOS variability, respectively. These findings demonstrate that interannual variability provides complementary information to long-term phenological trends and that SOS and EOS respond differently to climatic and environmental conditions.

title: Exploring Drivers of Structural Variability in Norway Spruce Stands Using Airborne LiDAR
summary: Airborne LiDAR provides a powerful framework for objectively describing forest structure across multiple spatial scales. From LiDAR points to a unit of area, to descriptors of individual trees, to cohorts of trees, to the stand, or at a landscape level, its analytical value can create a hierarchical understanding of drivers affecting the structural variability of trees and their spatial organisation on multiple levels. In this study, we analysed the structure of relatively pure Norway spruce (Picea abies (L.) Karst.) stands in the Ciucaș Mountains (Brașov County, Romania) using airborne LiDAR data. The point cloud was processed in R using an open-source workflow comprising ground classification, terrain modelling, height normalisation, canopy height modelling, treetop detection, and crown delineation. Structural metrics were derived hierarchically, from individual trees to summary statistics for tree cohorts within 500 m2 grid cells, and subsequently to stand-level statistics across grid cells within spruce stands. The geospatial dataset consisted of 58,708 grid cells grouped in 147 stands; for inferential analyses, a filtered dataset of 42,015 cells was retained, covering a total area of 2075.6 hectares. We applied a four-part analytical framework: (i) hierarchical mixed-effects models at the cell level, (ii) quantification of within-stand structural heterogeneity, (iii) stand-level structural typology based on principal component analysis and k-means clustering, and (iv) integration of disturbance history using combined Potapov (pre-2001) and Hansen (2001–2022) forest loss layers. The analysis revealed several patterns consistent with ecological expectations: mean canopy height increased with stand age, slope, and topographic position, whereas it decreased significantly with elevation. Canopy cover increased with elevation, slope, and topographic position, whereas the number of LiDAR-detected trees per cell increased with elevation but decreased with age and slope. The null model intraclass correlation coefficients ranged from 0.252 to 0.408, indicating appreciable between-stand variation alongside a larger within-stand residual component. Structural heterogeneity increased strongly with slope and, to a lesser extent, with northness. The stand typology identified five structural types: low-stature dense uniform, mid-height heterogeneous, tall closed uniform, tall open simplified, and very tall closed complex. Mapped tree cover loss occupied a small fraction of the retained forest sample and was associated with lower mean canopy height (approximately 1 m), lower canopy cover (approximately 4 percentage points), smaller mean crown area (approximately 2 m2), and a slightly lower number of LiDAR-detected trees per cell. These associations do not identify the causes of disturbance or its overall historical importance. In the Ciucaș Mountains, LiDAR-derived metrics provide a spatially explicit baseline for characterising spruce stand structure and its associations with stand age, topography, and mapped disturbance history.

title: Episodic Discharge Is the Dominant Correlate of Turbidity Variability in the Slave River Plume Zone of Great Slave Lake: Evidence from 40 Years of Satellite Observations
summary: Lake surface temperature (LST) and NDTI-based optical turbidity are important indicators of water quality and ecosystem dynamics in northern lakes, where climate warming and river discharge strongly influence thermal structure and sediment transport. This study used multi-sensor satellite observations processed in Google Earth Engine to examine long-term (1984–2024) variability in LST and NDTI-based optical turbidity within the Slave River–Great Slave Lake system, Northwest Territories, Canada, using Landsat, MODIS-Aqua and Sentinel-2 imagery. Landsat (1984–2024) and MODIS Aqua (2002–2024) indicated open-water warming of approximately +0.06 and +0.07 °C yr−1, respectively; only the Landsat trend was statistically significant (p = 0.038 versus p = 0.073). The Normalized Difference Turbidity Index (NDTI), used as a relative optical proxy for turbidity, exhibited strong interannual variability that co-varied primarily with Slave River discharge (MODIS Aqua r = 0.91, n = 23, t = 9.80; Landsat 1984–2024 r = 0.72, n = 41, t = 6.41; both p < 0.0001). Principal Component Analysis revealed discharge and NDTI-based optical turbidity as the dominant modes of variability, explaining 65% of the total variance, while LST loaded mainly on a separate component, accounting for a further 32%. The 2020 high-flow event produced the most extensive NDTI-based optical turbidity episode within the 40-year study period, with elevated NDTI consistently detected across all satellite platforms, followed by a marked decline through 2024. Monthly analysis revealed a discharge-dependent NDTI-based optical turbidity lag, with peak NDTI-based optical turbidity occurring concurrently with or within one month of peak discharge during high-flow years but delayed by up to 3–4 months during low-flow years. Spatial analyses further demonstrated persistent NDTI-based optical turbidity intensification near the Slave River mouth and the southwestern basin. These findings indicate that although LST shows a positive but sensor-dependent warming tendency, NDTI variability within the Slave River Plume Zone (SRPZ) was primarily associated with episodic high-discharge conditions consistent with sediment transport processes dominating optical water quality. The study further highlights the value of multi-sensor satellite observations for long-term environmental monitoring in remote subarctic lake systems.

title: Inventory-Constrained Monthly Mapping of China’s Sectoral CO2 Emissions at 1 Km Using Earth Observation and Emission-Source Data
summary: Kilometer-scale, sector-specific CO2 inventories support atmospheric modeling and regional mitigation. We developed an inventory-constrained monthly 1 km CO2 allocation product for China covering 2000–2024 and six sectors. Prescribed Emissions Database for Global Atmospheric Research (EDGAR) sector-month totals were conserved and spatially redistributed using sector-specific combinations of settlement, infrastructure, and emission-source data; the product therefore does not independently estimate aggregate emissions. Combined emissions increased from 3612.7 Mt CO2 in 2000 to 12,034.1 Mt CO2 in 2024, an increase of 233.1%. Evaluation against separate EDGAR gridmaps for 2024 assessed cell-magnitude agreement, spatial ranking, and top-10% hotspot overlap, but was only partially independent because of the shared EDGAR lineage. Buildings showed the strongest agreement within the residential benchmark scope (r = 0.906, ρ = 0.831; overlap = 70.6%), whereas power achieved only 12.0% positive-union overlap. Evaluations of transport and the industrial sectors were limited by benchmark compatibility. Comparison with the Global Emission Modeling System (GEMS) showed strong common-scope rank agreement (ρ = 0.834 in 2012 and 0.823 in 2021). The framework can be adapted to regions with compatible emission totals and spatial predictors, subject to region-specific evaluation.

title: Martian Mesospheric Gravity-Wave-Related Perturbations During Dust Storms Revealed by ACS-TGO Observations
summary: Gravity waves (GWs) are important for understanding the coupling between dust activity and atmospheric dynamics on Mars. Using temperature and water-vapor profiles from the Near-Infrared channel of the Atmospheric Chemistry Suite (ACS-NIR) onboard the ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter (TGO), we investigate wave-related temperature perturbations during global and regional dust-storm periods. Comparisons between Mars Years (MY) 34 and 35 reveal a localized enhancement of wave-related perturbations at southern high latitudes, particularly between 60°S and 90°S and 40–90 km. This enhancement persists after controlling for differences in observational sampling. The gravity-wave-related potential-energy proxy is approximately 2–3 times larger during the MY34 global dust storm, with a weaker enhancement during the regional event. These variations coincide with substantial differences in background temperature, static stability, and zonal winds, suggesting that dust-related changes in the atmospheric environment may modify wave propagation and filtering. Water-vapor abundance is also higher in the same region, but is more likely associated with dust-driven large-scale circulation, while wave-related processes may provide additional local modulation. These results provide observational constraints on dust–wave–water coupling in the Martian middle atmosphere.

title: Spatiotemporal Evolution of Mining-Induced Surface Subsidence in Thick Unconsolidated-Layer Coal–Cropland Overlapping Areas Using Multi-Temporal UAV LiDAR and Leveling Measurements
summary: Mining-induced subsidence affects cropland use and land management in coal–cropland overlapping areas. Leveling provides high-precision subsidence time series but limited spatial sampling, whereas multi-temporal unmanned aerial vehicle light detection and ranging (UAV LiDAR) provides spatially continuous terrain-change information, although the uncertainty of digital elevation model (DEM) differencing must be assessed. Three UAV LiDAR surveys (30 May 2025, 25 December 2025, and 14 June 2026) and leveling measurements (March 2025–April 2026) were combined to analyze subsidence at the 32311 working face of Xutuan Coal Mine, Anhui Province, China, during working-face advance and after mining cessation. The level of detection at the 95% confidence level (LoD95) was calculated from elevation residuals in stable areas, and LiDAR-derived subsidence was validated against leveling measurements at 12 points. The LoD95 values of the two cross-sensor differencing periods were 131.9 and 148.8 mm, indicating that changes smaller than approximately 0.13–0.15 m could not be reliably distinguished from measurement error in this study. Leveling-derived cumulative subsidence at these points ranged from 19.76 to 392.95 mm during 30 May–19 December 2025, comprising 19.76–69.75 mm at the six weak-subsidence points and 185.13–392.95 mm at the six strong-subsidence points. LiDAR-derived subsidence showed a strong relationship with leveling measurements at the six strong-subsidence points (R2 = 0.87, RMSE = 29.9 mm), whereas the relationship was weak at the six weak-subsidence points (R2 = 0.15). At seven representative leveling points, post-cessation residual subsidence accounted for 15.9–31.2% (mean 20.8%) of the final cumulative subsidence recorded during the leveling period. Relative to 30 May 2025, the area with subsidence exceeding 150 mm increased from 15.31 ha on 25 December 2025 to 16.73 ha on 14 June 2026. The two techniques thus provide complementary temporal and spatial information: leveling measurements reveal the persistence of post-cessation subsidence, while UAV LiDAR characterizes changes in the spatial distribution of cumulative subsidence. Continued monitoring after mining cessation is therefore necessary to capture ongoing surface movement and its spatial characteristics.

title: Improving Hail Diagnosis in Thunderstorms by Combining Radar and Lightning Detection Data
summary: Recent studies indicate an increasing frequency of hailstorms in the Mediterranean region, strengthening the need for improved monitoring and detection methods due to their impacts on human safety and socio-economic activities. This study proposes a real-time method for hail diagnosis in thunderstorms based on the joint use of X-band weather radars and lightning measurements. The approach integrates the Vertically Integrated Liquid Density (VILD) algorithm with a new version of the lightning jump algorithm (hail lightning jump), relating hail growth mechanisms to VILD maxima and lightning-derived variables. Hail reports were used to classify hailstorm severity and link hail occurrence with radar and lightning variables. The 31 confirmed hailstorms examined in Southern Italy show comparable sensitivity of the radar- and lightning-based methods, which identify 80.6% and 77.4% of the events, respectively. When combined using a logical “OR” configuration, the fraction of identified hail events increases to 93.5%. Lightning-based analysis over the Italian Peninsula shows higher lightning activity for very large hail events (≥5 cm) than for large hail cases (2–5 cm). A strong positive correlation between maximum hail size and lightning activity was also found. These results highlight the benefits of a combined approach and the crucial role of lightning activity in diagnosing hail formation and size in thunderstorms.

title: Contrasting Water-Partitioning Responses to Land-Use Change and Climate Perturbations in a Forested Mountain Catchment
summary: Forested mountain catchments play a critical role in regulating regional water resources, yet the effects of land-use change and precipitation–temperature perturbations on internal water partitioning and its seasonal and spatial variability remain insufficiently understood. In this study, we integrated remotely sensed land-cover information and MODIS-derived normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) with a calibrated and validated Soil and Water Assessment Tool (SWAT) model to examine hydrological sensitivities and non-additive responses under three land-use configurations and controlled climate perturbations in the upper Pi River Basin, China. Land-cover transitions affected only 2.7% of the study area and produced relatively small hydrological differences among land-use configurations, whereas a 20% precipitation increase enhanced soil-profile percolation (PERC) and surface runoff (SURQ) by 28.62% and 49.81%, respectively; 2 °C warming increased actual evapotranspiration (ET) by 3.58% but reduced SURQ by 5.39%. Under the combined scenario of 20% higher precipitation and 2 °C warming, ET and SURQ increased by 7.15% and 42.06%, respectively, with a non-additive SURQ deviation of −2.36 percentage points; ET sensitivity to precipitation peaked in August, coinciding with the NDVI maximum, whereas sensitivity to warming peaked in May, and soil water storage (SW) responses to warming differed in direction among subbasins. These findings reveal contrasting influences of precipitation supply and temperature-related evaporative demand on hydrological pathways, with component-specific non-additive effects and distinct seasonal and spatial responses. These patterns support the use of remotely sensed vegetation information and distributed hydrological modeling to identify climate-sensitive periods and evaluate spatial differences in water availability in forested mountain catchments.

title: Common Spatial Support and Registration Networks for Reproducible ArcticDEM Elevation Change Analysis
summary: Comparisons of elevation change from repeat digital elevation models (DEMs) depend on which pixels are evaluated and which DEM pairs are used for alignment. These effects were examined using ArcticDEM strips, four terrain windows with known perturbations, and four acquisitions at the Batagay megaslump. In the original single-realization tests, the maximum joint-gradient component and protected-change median errors were 0.087 and 0.027 m. In 480 additional paired perturbations, all joint-gradient estimates met the prescribed 0.50 m component tolerance; the median maximum component error was 0.026 m. On the observed Batagay terrain, joint-gradient, xDEM Nuth–Kääb, and historical internal Nuth–Kääb fits were accepted for 16, 17, and 14 of 18 pair-by-reference combinations, respectively, under matched candidate sampling. In the historical two-implementation comparison, restricting the combined-reference network to shared edges increased the July–September 2024 root-mean-square difference between the two change maps from 1.755 to 2.577 m on 184,120 identical target cells. Changing from pair-specific to fixed evaluation support had little effect on that interval. These results distinguish sensitivity to graph selection from sensitivity to the terrain evaluated. Independent elevations were unavailable at Batagay, so the outputs cannot be ranked by field accuracy.

title: Measurand-Aware Inter-Platform Consistency Assessment of GOES Land Surface Temperature Harmonization
summary: Cross-platform land surface temperature (LST) harmonization is often evaluated by agreement of individual observations, although urban analyses commonly rely on spatial differences and temporal changes. We investigated whether improving agreement in urban-core and surrounding-ring LST also improves their core–ring contrast and pre-to-post-sunset transition. Using Advanced Baseline Imager observations from Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites (GOES)-16, -17, -18, and -19 over western North American cities during 2019–2026, we evaluated five cohorts using established mean-squared-error (MSE) decomposition and cross-validated model selection at each measurand. Component root-mean-squared error (RMSE) decreased by 29.3–59.7%, whereas core–ring contrast RMSE ranged from an 11.5% reduction to a 13.1% increase. Loss of residual covariance offset 94.6–114.0% of gross variance-plus-bias gains. In the post hoc 2026 temporal evaluation of the same 75 cities used for 2025 calibration, core and ring RMSE declined by 59.7% and 56.1%, but contrast RMSE reduction was −0.14% (95% crossed city–interval bootstrap interval, −6.75% to +6.48%, with cities and intervals resampled independently). The historical 2021 evaluation likewise showed only a small, uncertain contrast improvement (2.9%; 95% interval, −4.3% to +9.8%). Calibration-based selection retained raw contrasts and transitions, while a residual interval rule withheld uncertain transition direction claims. Independent three-station radiometric comparisons assessed raw satellite products at station scale rather than the complete urban workflow. These findings demonstrate why harmonization performance should be evaluated at the derived scientific quantity, with processing decisions based on its observed cross-platform consistency.

title: Enhanced Chlorophyll Responses to the Interaction Between an Anticyclonic Eddy and Internal Solitary Waves: A Case Study
summary: Mesoscale eddies and internal solitary waves (ISWs) influence upper-ocean chlorophyll variability, yet their roles in the spatial variations in chlorophyll during their interaction remain poorly revealed. Using satellite ocean-color and sunglint imagery, we observed different chlorophyll variabilities in three cases: an ISW-only case, an eddy-only case, and an eddy–ISW interaction case. In the ISW-only case, chlorophyll exhibited coherent, banded, and phase-dependent anomalies, characterized by reduced concentrations near the wave trough but enhanced ones in the trailing region, with a chlorophyll anomaly reaching approximately 0.02 mg m−3. In the eddy-only case, chlorophyll exhibited a distinct low-core but high-periphery structure, with elevated filamentary features concentrated around the eddy boundary and spatially consistent with enhanced finite-size Lyapunov exponent (FSLE). During the eddy–ISW interaction, the ISW crests became strongly deformed near the eddy periphery, consistent with modulation by the mesoscale eddy. Within the eddy interior, the ISW-related banded chlorophyll structure remained evident, whereas near the eddy periphery these bands became curved and spatially overlapped with filamentary chlorophyll structures. The difference in chlorophyll between the eddy–ISW and eddy-only cases increased toward the eddy periphery, reaching approximately 50% at ~1.2R. These observations reveal a multiscale spatial modulation of chlorophyll variability, in which the mesoscale eddy establishes a broader spatial pattern, while ISWs induce propagating fine-scale perturbations. The eddy–ISW interaction primarily regulates and enhances chlorophyll variability near the eddy periphery, rather than producing a uniform response throughout the eddy.

title: PMA-SAM2: Prior-Memory Adapted Framework for Automatic Remote Sensing Water Body Extraction
summary: SAM2 has great potential for remote sensing water body extraction due to its strong feature representation capability. However, when directly applied to the water body segmentation task, SAM2 still faces several challenges, including domain discrepancy, spectral confusion between water bodies and shadow-like objects, significant intra-class variations, and dependence on manual prompts. To address these challenges, this paper proposes the PMA-SAM2, which integrates domain prior injection, prototype memory calibration, and automatic prompt guidance for robust water body extraction. First, a Multi-level Prior Adaptation Module is designed to inject spatial geometric information and texture features into the SAM2 encoder, enabling effective alignment between general visual representations and remote sensing domain features. Then, a Prototype Memory Calibration Module is introduced to dynamically accumulate water feature prototypes under different geographical environments and imaging conditions, improving the model’s robustness to intra-class variations and inter-class spectral ambiguity. Furthermore, an Automatic Prompt Decoder is proposed to transform prototype-retrieved similarity maps into dense prompts, replacing manual prompts and enabling fully automatic water body segmentation. Experimental results on four datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior water body extraction accuracy compared with mainstream segmentation methods, verifying its strong generalization capability and scene adaptability.

title: Source Characteristics of the 2025 Mw 6.0 Aheqi Earthquake: Possible Relationship to the 2024 Mw 7.0 Wushi Earthquake
summary: The 4 December 2025 Mw 6.0 Aheqi earthquake occurred on the Maidan–Shayilamusi Fault system in the western southern Tian Shan, approximately 23 months after the 2024 Mw 7.0 Wushi earthquake. We used ascending- and descending-track Sentinel-1A differential interferometric synthetic aperture radar (DInSAR) observations to map coseismic line-of-sight (LOS) deformation, jointly invert fault geometry and distributed slip, calculate Coulomb failure stress changes, and evaluate sequence association using earthquake-catalog statistics and an epidemic-type aftershock sequence (ETAS) model. The deformation field is elongated NEE–SWW, with maximum displacement toward the satellite of approximately 6 cm. The preferred model has a strike of 242°, dip of 40°, rake of 77°, and maximum slip of 0.21 m concentrated at depths of 4.89–7.46 km, corresponding to Mw 5.91. The joint inversion yields an RMSE of 0.0145 m. Coulomb stress calculations indicate positive ΔCFS at the Aheqi source within the principal rupture-depth interval of 4.89–7.46 km across all three tested receiver-fault geometries. For the preferred geometry, ΔCFS reaches +6.16 bar at the slip-centroid depth of 6.18 km and is close to zero (+0.29 bar) at 10 km, where its sign varies among the tested geometries. At 15 km, ΔCFS is negative for all three geometries. ETAS stochastic declustering assigns the Aheqi event a total triggered-component probability of 82.6% and a background-component probability of 17.4%. Separate attribution analysis yields a 65.7% probability of belonging to the Wushi mainshock’s descendant sequence and a 0.5% probability of direct triggering by the Wushi mainshock. Together with the spatiotemporal compatibility of the two events, these results support a possible interaction within the segmented Maidan–Shayilamusi Fault system, although they do not establish deterministic causation or uniquely identify the physical triggering pathway. The modeled stress pattern also highlights nearby positively loaded fault segments for continued monitoring.

title: FVE: Fire-Management-Aligned Vision–Language Reasoning for UAV-Based Fire-Event Assessment
summary: Existing unmanned aerial vehicle fire monitoring methods primarily recognize visible smoke or flame cues but cannot reliably determine whether an observed anomaly is an uncontrolled fire requiring intervention. This study reformulates UAV fire monitoring from a conventional visual-recognition problem into an event-level reasoning and decision task. We propose Fire-Verify-Expert (FVE), a compact vision–language model that jointly performs smoke and fire cue confirmation, real-fire verification, event-type attribution, and ordered response-priority assessment. FVE incorporates fire-management logic into multimodal preference alignment through a multidimensional Group Relative Policy Optimization objective. Its reward mechanism constrains determination correctness, event-type consistency, rationale–decision consistency, and reasoning quality, while imposing asymmetric penalties on operationally costly errors, particularly missed real fires and severe underestimation of response priority. To support this task, we establish a UAV-oriented dataset of 600 images spanning varied environmental contexts and viewing perspectives, including real fires and visually similar controlled or currently non-actionable smoke/fire events. The dataset provides structured reasoning annotations and ordered response-priority labels. FVE achieves an accuracy/F1-score of 0.917/0.915 for real-fire verification, with a recall of 1.000 for real fires, and an accuracy/F1-score of 0.833/0.706 for response-priority assessment. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of FVE in aligning multimodal vision–language reasoning with fire-management requirements, providing a feasible approach for automated fire-event verification and response prioritization in frontline UAV fire-monitoring workflows.

title: Spatially Aware Uncertainty Feedback for Hard Region Learning in Remote Sensing Semantic Segmentation
summary: Remote sensing semantic segmentation often produces spatially concentrated errors around object boundaries, small targets, shadowed areas, and ambiguous land-cover transitions. This study investigates whether learned spatial uncertainty can guide additional supervision of such difficult pixels. We propose Spatially Aware Uncertainty Feedback for Hard Region Learning (SUF-HRL), which refines a maximum-softmax-probability prior through a residual uncertainty branch attached to a SegFormer backbone. Local alignment and boundary concentration objectives encourage a task-adaptive spatial difficulty map; after a warm-up stage, its highest-scoring pixels receive additional cross-entropy supervision. Experiments use the Potsdam and Vaihingen benchmarks of the International Society for Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing and the LoveDA land-cover dataset. Under the controlled SegFormer-B2 protocol, mean intersection over union (mIoU) increases by 0.69, 1.14, and 1.01 percentage points, respectively. Averaging boundary-region mIoU over 3-, 5-, and 7-pixel bands gives gains of approximately 1.44, 1.32, and 1.32 percentage points. Component ablations support contributions from both spatial objectives. Learned uncertainty improves the reported spatial uncertainty criteria on Vaihingen, although it does not achieve the best precision–recall or calibration score. On Potsdam, training time per iteration increases by approximately 68.5% while the reported parameter totals remain nearly unchanged. The additional inference latency is small in the tested configuration. These results support learned spatial uncertainty as a useful training signal for hard-region segmentation.

title: Characterizing Correspondence Coverage Collapse in UAV RGB–TIR Registration
summary: Registration quality in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) RGB and thermal infrared (TIR) imagery is often assessed using reprojection error, although low residuals at the correspondences used for estimation do not necessarily indicate reliable alignment across the common image footprint. This study investigates Correspondence Coverage Collapse as a diagnostic pattern in which low in-sample error coexists with concentrated correspondences, limited spatial support, and poorer held-out performance. Seventeen RGB–TIR image pairs were analyzed using a two-stage common-footprint normalization and a fixed full-inlier correspondence pool generated by SuperPoint–SuperGlue. Clustered, Random, and Balanced subsets were compared under equal correspondence budgets, with common held-out correspondences used for generalization assessment. At N=80, Clustered selection achieved the lowest selected-point RMSE but showed the highest held-out RMSE, lowest spatial coverage, and largest reference-grid deviation. Confidence-ranked selection showed a similar but weaker pattern at lower correspondence budgets. Continuous analyses further showed that lower coverage and greater distance-to-support were associated with higher held-out error and global transformation deviation. These results indicate that reprojection error alone does not characterize spatial support or held-out performance within the evaluated correspondence pool.

title: Interpretable Coseismic Landslide Susceptibility Assessment Using an Explainable Boosting Machine: A Case Study of the 2022 Luding Earthquake, China
summary: Earthquake-induced landslide susceptibility assessment is important for post-earthquake hazard identification and risk mitigation. However, conventional machine learning models often provide limited insight into their prediction mechanisms. This study applies the Explainable Boosting Machine (EBM) to landslides triggered by the 5 September 2022 Luding earthquake and investigates the nonlinear responses and interactions of the controlling factors. Conditioning factors were screened through correlation and multicollinearity analyses, and the key model parameters were optimized using grid search. The final model included nine main effects and 36 pairwise interactions to characterize nonlinear factor responses and joint effects. The EBM achieved AUC values of 0.987 and 0.976 for the training and testing datasets, respectively, while both Accuracy and F1-score reached 0.920 on the testing dataset. The susceptibility map was classified into five levels using the Natural Breaks method, and the frequency ratio increased from 0.01 in the very low susceptibility class to 6.74 in the very high susceptibility class. Elevation, PGA, and Lithology were the three most important main effects, with importance scores of 1.836, 1.512, and 1.324, respectively. Lithology × PGA and Elevation × Lithology showed the strongest pairwise interactions, indicating that the effects of seismic shaking and elevation on landslide susceptibility were strongly modified by lithological conditions. These results demonstrate that EBM can characterize coseismic landslide susceptibility patterns while directly revealing nonlinear factor responses and pairwise interactions, providing an interpretable framework for understanding the combined influences of seismic, geological, and topographic conditions on landslide susceptibility.

title: Observation-Integrity- and Geometry-Aware SimVP-RD for Irregular PS-InSAR Deformation Forecasting of Earth-Rockfill Dams
summary: PS-InSAR provides spatially distributed line-of-sight (LOS) deformation measurements, creating an opportunity to forecast dam-surface deformation as a spatial field rather than at isolated monitoring points. However, irregular acquisition intervals, sparse observations, and anisotropic radar pixels complicate multi-step forecasting. We develop SimVP-RD, an observation-integrity- and geometry-aware framework that predicts reference-interval increments, scales them by the actual elapsed time, and integrates them from the latest observed field. The framework combines fixed-support masking, a reconstruction-dynamics objective, native-grid anisotropic convolution, and recursive rollout training. Using 94 real acquisitions of Lianghekou Dam, SimVP-RD achieves an MAE of 3.355 ± 0.024 mm and an RMSE of 4.534 ± 0.034 mm under a matched observed-only 8→8 recursive protocol, outperforming ConvLSTM, PredRNN, and TAU. The corrected Stage-A ablation further shows that the reconstruction-dynamics objective reduces MAE from 3.833 ± 0.111 to 3.549 ± 0.086 mm. On the native PS grid, the 3 × 7 convolution retains all 2170 valid locations and provides a more balanced physical receptive field than the conventional 3 × 3 kernel. Spatial and interval-stratified diagnostics further characterize how forecast errors vary across prediction leads and spatial contexts. These results establish SimVP-RD as a support-preserving approach to multi-step LOS deformation-field forecasting under irregular satellite sampling.

title: EORENet: Edge-Optimized Road Extraction from 2 m GF-1 Imagery for Large-Area Road Mapping
summary: Accurate road extraction from high-resolution satellite imagery is important for transportation planning, infrastructure monitoring, and geospatial updating, but blurred boundaries and fragmented segments still limit practical large-area applications. This study proposes EORENet, an edge-optimized road extraction network for 2 m GF-1 imagery and large-area road product generation. EORENet decouples road-surface segmentation and road-edge delineation into task-specific branches, introduces deformable convolution for adaptive spatial aggregation, and uses a dual-task cross-feature fusion module to exchange semantic and boundary cues. A GF-1 road sample set, the Cangling Road Dataset, was constructed and evaluated together with the Ottawa and DeepGlobe Road datasets. Compared with eight representative methods, EORENet achieved the best overall IoU, F1 score, and edge-buffered F1 score; on the Cangling dataset, it reached 55.11% IoU, 71.06% F1, and 56.21% edge-buffered F1. The trained model was then applied to a spatially independent large-area GF-1 inference collection. Scene-stratified product-level assessment with 1200 independently annotated 512 × 512 patches showed systematic scene-dependent differences, with F1 scores ranging from 62.80% in mountainous forest areas to 74.57% in high-density urban cores and a balanced scene-wise mean F1 of 69.48%. City-scale extraction over four metropolitan regions further visually illustrated the workflow’s potential for large-area road-surface product generation.

title: TSD-LitePT: Transition-Sensitive Detail Enhancement for UAV LiDAR Transmission-Corridor Segmentation
summary: UAV-borne LiDAR segmentation of transmission corridors is hindered by the anisotropic geometry of elongated conductors, semantic ambiguity near component junctions, and the loss of sparse insulator evidence during hierarchical sampling. To address these challenges, we propose TSD-LitePT, a three-stage extension of LitePT. First, Learnable Axial Rotary Position Encoding learns independent scales for the x-, y-, and z-axis rotary phases, adapting positional sensitivity to corridor geometry. Second, Transition-Modulated Semantic Refinement derives a segmentation-driven point-wise response from decoded features and uses it to gate semantic residuals, refining ambiguous representations without boundary annotations. Third, Sparse-Target Detail Calibration uses decoded semantics, normalized coordinates, and transition context to calibrate shallow high-resolution features, then aggregates serialized-neighborhood evidence into an insulator prior. A bounded, confidence-aware residual injects this prior into the insulator logit while suppressing changes at confident non-target points. Across three runs on the original five-class corridor dataset, TSD-LitePT achieved an mIoU of 0.9200±0.0003 and an insulator IoU of 0.7236±0.0016 (mean ± standard deviation), compared with 0.8818±0.0061 and 0.5548±0.0435, respectively, for LitePT. After separate retraining on an independent transmission corridor, TSD-LitePT achieved an mIoU of 0.8909, compared with 0.8653 for LitePT. The largest improvement occurred for insulators, while power-line and ground performance remained close to the baseline. These results show that coordinating positional adaptation, semantic refinement, and controlled detail recovery improves minority-component segmentation without disturbing dominant classes.

title: Monthly Multi-Source Remote Sensing Reveals Seasonal Pulses, Bundle Transitions, and Differentiated Management of Ecosystem Services in the Yongding River Basin
summary: Seasonal basin management requires knowing when ecosystem services coincide and how their configurations differ among subbasins, information that annual summaries can obscure. We integrated monthly remote sensing, meteorological, soil, and terrain data to estimate carbon fixation (CF), water conservation (WC), soil retention (SR), and wind erosion prevention (WEP) in 18 Yongding River subbasins in 2018, 2020, and 2023. Seasonal association networks and a self-organizing map characterized 648 subbasin–month service profiles and their bundle histories. Of 648 monthly bundle labels, 237 (36.6%) differed from the label of the corresponding annual mean service vector. The high-CF–WC–SR bundle occurred in 26 monthly profiles, including 19 of 54 July observations, whereas subbasin 4 retained a WEP-oriented bundle in 30 of 36 sampled months. In the three-year mean seasonal profiles, 12 of 18 subbasins shared a summer CF-enhanced pathway; the other six followed alternative pathways. CF, WC, and SR were generally higher in summer, while WEP peaked in April and was more prominent in western and southwestern subbasins. Seasonal networks showed the strongest screened association for winter SR–WC, while the summer WC–WEP confidence interval crossed zero. Together, monthly bundle histories and seasonal association networks identify shared summer assessment windows and subbasin-specific priorities for spring wind exposure and service-bundle transition monitoring, providing spatially and temporally explicit evidence for differentiated seasonal management in the Yongding River Basin.

title: Three Decades of Ground Deformation at Somma–Vesuvio (Italy) from Multi-Mission DInSAR Time Series (1993–2024): Insights from Time-Series Inspection and Variational Bayesian Independent Component Analysis
summary: We analyse three decades of ground displacement time series at Somma–Vesuvio volcano (Italy), derived from a multi-mission Differential Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (DInSAR) dataset combining ERS/ENVISAT (1993–2010), RADARSAT-2 (2010–2015), and Sentinel-1 (2015–2024) acquisitions. The DInSAR measurements are referenced to a site at Marigliano, approximately 12 km north of the summit, and are validated against continuous GNSS observations and analysed at representative sites spanning the summit area, the circum-Vesuvian ring, eastern Naples, and the volcanic apron. In addition, we apply Variational Bayesian Independent Component Analysis jointly to quasi-vertical and eastward displacements within 16 km of the summit. The results identify (i) a spatially confined, exponentially decaying subsidence transient along the circum-Vesuvian ring, previously identified from shorter ERS/ENVISAT time series; (ii) deformation in eastern Naples consistent with post-industrial groundwater rebound; (iii) a marked change in the regional deformation regime around 2001–2002, also previously identified from shorter ERS/ENVISAT time series; and (iv) a progressive subsidence slowdown after approximately 2014–2015, particularly along the southern flank. Together, the spatial and temporal coherence of these signals with published seismic, tilt, fumarolic, and groundwater–geochemical observations supports the interpretation of a persistent deep-seated contribution to the long-term deformation of the volcano, while the vbICA decomposition demonstrates that substantial shallow and anthropogenic contributions are superimposed on the volcanic signal. More generally, the results show that long-term multi-mission DInSAR combined with statistical source separation can help disentangle coexisting deformation processes in complex volcanic environments.

title: STC-PFTF-Net: Structure-Guided Prior Fusion for Cover-Crop Canopy Delineation in Residue-Rich UAV Imagery
summary: Delineating early cover-crop vegetation in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery requires preserving slender leaves amid cast shadows, desiccated residue, and heterogeneous soil. Weak foliage contrast and leaf-like background edges make appearance and geometry jointly important. We propose the Shadow, Topology, and Chromatic-aware Prior Feature Topology Fusion Network (STC-PFTF-Net), which integrates structure-guided reconstruction with complementary appearance representations. A coherence-guided tangent–normal decomposition preserves tangential sampling displacement and attenuates displacement across local structures. Chromatic–photometric encoding, directional wavelet filtering, and local connectivity refinement support this reconstruction throughout the feature hierarchy. On the 32 validation tiles of the Residue-rich Cover-Crop UAV Dataset, drawn from an area spatially separated from training, STC-PFTF-Net achieves 77.71% foreground intersection over union (IoU), 50.88% Boundary IoU, 83.84% centerline Dice (clDice), and 87.35% F1. At a common decision threshold, the complete model also exceeds the comparison architectures in all four measures. Spatial analyses associate its higher boundary recall with vegetation–background transitions and identify low-greenness foliage as a distinct source of omission. These findings show the value of combining appearance information with explicit reconstruction geometry for fine-scale canopy delineation. With 2.12 million parameters, the model offers a compact representation for UAV-derived vegetation mapping and subsequent canopy-cover assessment.

title: SAGE-Map: Structure–Appearance Guided Calibration and Geometry Refinement for Satellite-Derived High-Definition Maps
summary: High-resolution satellite imagery supports scalable mapping, but dense-to-vector pipelines can misrank overlapping candidates and retain local geometric errors. We present SAGE-Map, a framework for structure–appearance guided calibration and geometry refinement built on our SAM-Road-based pipeline for OpenSatMap20. The baseline extracts Lane, Curb, and Virtual polylines with normal-displacement correction. SAGE-Map combines structural scoring with candidate-aligned DINOv2 evidence to rescore Lane candidates, then trims unsupported endpoints while preserving candidate identity, class, and count. On 393 validation tiles, SAGE-Map achieves 29.27, 31.33, 34.06, and 36.06% Chamfer average precision at 0.9, 1.5, 3.0, and 4.5 m, respectively, and 46.78% mean intersection over union (mIoU). Under our reconstructed implementation of the published protocol, these point estimates are higher than reported UniMapGen aggregates; no paired statistical comparison with UniMapGen is available. Paired bootstrap intervals for gains over our baseline are positive through 3.0 m but cross zero at 4.5 m. Post hoc component comparisons associate most of the strict-tolerance gain with rescoring and the mIoU gain with endpoint trimming. Additional geometric analysis shows lower forward distance but worse symmetric distance and reduced GT length coverage after trimming. The gains therefore concern the evaluated ranking and overlap metrics, rather than general geometric completeness.

title: Pre-Launch Assessment of Simulated CHIME and LSTM Data for Water-Quality Monitoring in a Virtual Constellation Framework
summary: The use of Earth Observation data for monitoring of aquatic and coastal ecosystems has expanded significantly, yet gaps remain in the spectral and thermal capabilities needed to detect and characterize liquid discharges. This study evaluates the potential of simulated pre-launch CHIME and LSTM observations, integrated with operational Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8/9 data, for water-quality anomaly detection across diverse aquatic environments, demonstrating that the simulated datasets are sufficiently realistic to reproduce key water-quality and thermal indicators and support pre-operational application development prior to mission launch. A multi-stage workflow was applied: initial anomaly detection with multispectral imagery, thermal verification using LSTM-simulated brightness temperatures processed via linear and quadratic split-window algorithms, and spectral characterization of turbidity and spectral signatures with atmospherically corrected CHIME-simulated data. Results showed consistent spatial patterns of turbidity and surface temperature between simulated and operational products, with CHIME resolving finer spectral features of suspended matter and the quadratic LSTM model achieving low RMSE relative to Landsat thermal references. These findings demonstrate the cross-sensor consistency and complementary information provided by simulated CHIME and LSTM products, supporting their use in the pre-launch development of future multisensor workflows for detecting and characterizing optical and thermal water anomalies. Identification of specific contaminants and attribution of anomalies to individual discharge sources were not assessed in this study.

title: Monitoring Vertical Deformation of Artificial Islands’ Boundary Structures Using Satellite InSAR and Geotechnical Back-Analysis
summary: Artificial islands developed through large-scale coastal reclamation require continuous monitoring to ensure long-term geotechnical stability and infrastructure safety. This study presents an integrated framework combining multi-temporal Persistent Scatterer Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (PSI) with numerical geotechnical modelling to assess vertical deformation of boundary structures at Jumeirah Bay Island, Dubai. Copernicus Sentinel-1 data (2015–2023) were processed to derive high-resolution deformation time series, revealing millimetre-scale settlement patterns across the island’s seawalls, breakwaters, and quay walls. The results indicate cumulative settlements of up to 20 mm, with spatial variability linked to structural configuration, wave exposure, and loading conditions. Integration of satellite-derived deformation measurements with finite element modelling enabled the development of a calibration-constrained, scenario-based settlement projection to 2100 for the boundary structures of the reclaimed island, predicting additional creep settlement of up to 8.5 mm by 2100 for the industrial-building load category. The study extends previous InSAR-based investigations of reclaimed-land settlement by applying a structure-specific framework to artificial-island boundary systems and developing a long-term engineering projection constrained by satellite observations.

title: Training-Informed Differentiable Bayesian Inference with PROSPECT for Leaf Trait Retrieval and Uncertainty Analysis
summary: Leaf radiative transfer models provide a physical basis for leaf trait retrieval, but compensating parameter effects and measurement discrepancies constrain estimation accuracy and uncertainty characterization. This study proposes Training-Informed Differentiable Bayesian Inference (TI-DBI). This method integrates training-derived joint lognormal priors, wavelength-specific spectral biases, and residual scales into a differentiable PROSPECT-D model, enabling joint parameter inference via the No-U-Turn Sampler (NUTS). Evaluated on multi-source datasets, TI-DBI yields relative root mean square errors (rRMSEs) of 27.31%, 33.72%, 16.22%, and 37.66% for chlorophyll (Cab), carotenoids (Car), equivalent water thickness (Cw), and leaf dry mass per area (Cm). Outperforming an uncalibrated Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) baseline for all traits and partial least squares regression (PLSR) for Cab, Car, and Cw, these results confirm the specific value of the data-informed probabilistic framework. Beyond point-estimation, TI-DBI substantially improves uncertainty characterization. It yields narrower interval widths and lower interval scores than the uncalibrated baseline, with prediction interval coverage probability (PICP) of the 95% highest density intervals (HDIs) reaching 93.14%, 96.46%, 89.62%, and 86.22% for Cab, Car, Cw, and Cm, respectively. Ablation and sensitivity studies confirm that both the learned priors and spectral error calibration drive these performance gains across varying training fractions and spectral configurations. TI-DBI strictly preserves the forward model’s physical structure while providing a robust, practical framework for jointly evaluating trait estimation accuracy and posterior uncertainty.

title: Urbanization in Coastal Chilean Cities: Spatial Monitoring and Impact Assessment Using Sentinel Satellites
summary: We integrate Sentinel-1 P-SBAS InSAR (2019–2023), continuous GNSS and Sentinel-2 multitemporal urban-footprint data to characterize surface deformation in three Chilean coastal cities (30–38°S) on contrasting substrates: La Serena, Valparaíso and Concepción. A regional velocity field emerges, modulated by postseismic relaxation of the 2010 Maule and 2015 Illapel earthquakes. After GNSS correction, line-of-sight (LOS) velocities reach −30.5 mm/yr in Concepción, and points with |LOS| > 5 mm/yr are about eight times more frequent in Valparaíso (3.1%) and Concepción (3.3%) than in La Serena (0.4%), independently of point density. Negative velocities concentrate on Quaternary deposits at peripheral expansion fronts, including wetland margins in Concepción, with basement and urban cores stable. By 2020, built-up area on mapped wetlands reached 48, 7 and 3 ha in Concepción, Valparaíso and La Serena, respectively, rising to 60, 7 and 4 ha by 2030 (1.6%, 0.3%, 0.2%). The spatial distribution of deformation is therefore spatially associated with unconsolidated, low-lying substrates rather than with tectonic position, although groundwater extraction cannot be excluded as a contributing mechanism. Substrates of the same type failed in Concepción in 2010; continued expansion onto low-lying wetlands may increase the exposure of the built environment to both slow ground deformation and earthquake-induced ground failure, which warrants further geotechnical assessment.

title: Comparison Between TROPOMI and MAX-DOAS Tropospheric NO2 Observations in Shihezi: Sensitivity to Spatiotemporal Collocation
summary: Ground-based and satellite observations differ in temporal sampling and spatial representativeness, making collocation strategy important for satellite–ground comparisons. We analyzed MAX-DOAS observations in Shihezi, Xinjiang, China, from 5 June to 31 August 2023 together with Sentinel-5P/TROPOMI tropospheric NO2 vertical column density (VCD) products. Five temporal windows (closest observation, ±30 min, ±1 h, ±1.5 h, and ±2 h) and five spatial schemes (nearest pixel, 3 × 3- and 5 × 5-pixel averages, and across-track and along-track adjacent three-pixel averages) formed 25 collocation configurations. NO2 VCD increased during the morning and gradually decreased in the afternoon, while a representative enhancement episode during 12–16 July was concentrated mainly below 1 km. Across the 25 configurations, R ranged from 0.718 to 0.852, whereas NMB ranged from −42.84% to −32.33%, demonstrating that relatively strong temporal correlation did not imply close agreement in absolute VCD. Wider temporal windows generally reduced RMSE and MAE but did not produce corresponding increases in R. The ±30 min window combined with the along-track three-pixel average produced the highest R among the tested configurations and showed comparatively stable performance, although it was not statistically superior to all alternatives. Applying the TROPOMI tropospheric averaging kernel to the MAX-DOAS profiles increased R from 0.852 to 0.879 and reduced the magnitude of NMB from 33.76% to 5.04%. Nearest-pixel-center distance (0.40–6.81 km) was only weakly associated with the relative absolute difference (R = 0.31). These findings demonstrate that collocation choices materially affect TROPOMI–MAX-DOAS consistency and should be evaluated by jointly considering physical representativeness and multiple statistical metrics.

title: Performance of Selected Sampling Methods for Growing Stock Volume Estimation in Model-Based Two-Phase Forest Inventory
summary: Selection of an adequate sampling method is perhaps one of the most crucial stages of any survey. Researchers and decision-makers often face difficulties in selecting appropriate sampling techniques and sample sizes in relation to the specific research problem and the desired accuracy of estimates. Although general rules of thumb are relatively well established, the optimization of these elements is often based on rough approximations. Direct comparisons of the accuracy of different sampling methods in large-scale, real-world forest inventories are, in most cases, not practically feasible. Consequently, some studies rely on resampling limited observational datasets, whereas others generate artificial populations from which predefined samples can be drawn to evaluate sampling efficiency. Nevertheless, such populations tend to be simplified representations of the often complex structures of real forests. This study proposes an approach that could serve as a bridge between real and artificial data. Specifically, the efficiency of three popular sampling designs—simple random sampling (SRS), systematic sampling (SYS), and stratified sampling (StrS)—was compared for growing stock volume (GSV) estimation in a two-phase model-based forest inventory. The comparisons were performed using semi-synthetic forest populations, in which only the target variable was generated using a machine-learning approach, whereas all other parameters were derived from real forest inventory and remote sensing (RS) data. Stratification and sampling were performed using hierarchical data clustering and the concept of structurally guided sampling (SGS), which, in addition to sampling in geographical space, enables sampling in the multidimensional space of auxiliary variables. The proposed stratification technique allows for potentially more effective delineation of strata than predefined spatial layers, which should be crucial for the overall inventory performance. The results showed that hierarchical stratification (clustering) combined with SGS in the airborne laser scanning (ALS) data space was competitive with SRS and SYS, and could even outperform them at lower sampling intensity levels. The convergence zone in the accuracy and precision of SGS-GSV estimates could be reached at lower sampling intensities than with the classical sampling methods. These results demonstrate a potential for optimizing sampling in ALS model-based forest inventories and highlight opportunities for reducing sample sizes, without practically compromising the accuracy and precision of GSV estimates at the forest district level. Nonetheless, further validation on real-world datasets is needed, as synthetic populations may not fully capture the heterogeneity of actual forest structures, which would most likely require more intensive sampling. Therefore, the results presented in this study should be regarded as indicative of potential trends rather than as definitive guidelines for conducting remote sensing-supported forest inventories.

title: Short-Campaign GNSS Observations of Horizontal Velocity and Vertical Tidal Response Across the Drygalski Ice Tongue, East Antarctica
summary: The Drygalski Ice Tongue is a tide-influenced floating extension of the David Glacier in East Antarctica, where field observations are constrained by polar logistics. We investigated how horizontal ice motion and vertical tidal response vary along and across the tongue. To extend earlier observations, we analysed a 2025–2026 Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) campaign comprising 12 stations and 248 station-days. Kinematic GNSS coordinate series were produced with Bernese 5.4 and subsequently analysed under four stochastic covariance descriptions for horizontal and apparent vertical-rate estimation. Comparisons with a regional Mario Zucchelli Station (MZS)/Terra Nova Bay tide reference characterized station-level up-component response to tidal forcing, and two tide-removal paths were evaluated for apparent vertical-rate analysis. Floating-tongue speeds increased downstream, spanning 663.9–749.4 m/yr, with a clockwise turn toward the southeast and north-to-south differences in fitted campaign rates. The main horizontal patterns persisted across all four tested covariance descriptions. Vertical tidal response was weak in the near-grounding group, spatially heterogeneous in the transition sector, and near-unity downstream. Across the four covariance descriptions, neither tide-removal approach yielded a model-robust apparent vertical-rate field. The campaign resolved spatial patterns of horizontal motion and vertical tidal response, while covariance testing identified the limits of apparent vertical-rate inference from short GNSS records.

title: Spatiotemporal Patterns and Driving Factors of Carbon Emissions from Forest Fires in Heilongjiang Province, China (2001–2022)
summary: Forest fires are an important disturbance to the carbon cycle of terrestrial ecosystems and a major source of regional carbon emissions. This study used the emission factor method to estimate forest fire CO2, CO, and CH4 emissions in Heilongjiang Province from 2001 to 2022. The geographically and temporally weighted regression (GTWR) model was applied to examine spatiotemporal heterogeneity in the relationships between driving factors and CO2 emissions. Cumulative CO2, CO, and CH4 emissions were 72.95 Tg, 5171.73 Gg, and 246.54 Gg, respectively. Mean emissions per hectare of burned forest were 32.02, 2.27, and 0.108 Mg ha−1 for CO2, CO, and CH4, respectively. Emissions of all three gases showed significant downward trends (p < 0.001) and a bimodal monthly pattern with spring and autumn peaks. Deciduous broadleaf forests contributed 95.6% of CO2 emissions. Spatially, CO2 emissions were higher in the north than in the south and exhibited significant spatial clustering. The GTWR model achieved an adjusted R2 of 0.585, and fractional vegetation cover was the main influencing factor among the variables examined. Forest fire carbon emission estimates remain subject to some uncertainty. The results provide scientific support for regional forest fire risk management and forest fire carbon emission mitigation.

title: Discrepancies and Consistencies in Multi-Source Estimates of Eurasian Spring Snowmelt During 1982–2014
summary: Snow alters land–atmosphere energy and moisture exchanges via albedo and hydrological effects, markedly impacting subseasonal-to-seasonal climate variability. While Earth observations and model-based products form the foundation for investigating snow–climate interactions, comprehensive assessments of snowmelt, which directly reflects snow-induced hydrological and thermal anomalies, remain scarce compared to those of conventional snow mass variables. Benchmarked against the satellite–in situ blended GlobSnow data, this study comprehensively evaluates the discrepancies and consistencies of Eurasian spring snowmelt (spring snow water equivalent difference, SSD) across six multi-source datasets (SnowCCI, JRA-3Q, ERA5-Land, MERRA-2, GLDAS-NOAH, and FLDAS) during 1982–2014. The results reveal that satellite-based SnowCCI and JRA-3Q exhibit the highest consistency with GlobSnow in reproducing the spatial distribution, temporal variability, and dominant east–west dipole mode of Eurasian SSD. Specifically, they accurately capture its clear latitudinal zonation and a distinct dipole-like trend, characterized by decreasing SSD over western Eurasia and increasing SSD over eastern Eurasia. Conversely, ERA5-Land and MERRA-2 reasonably capture the temporal evolution of SSD but tend to overestimate variability amplitudes. GLDAS-NOAH exhibits relatively weak regional heterogeneity and underestimates SSD variability, whereas FLDAS tends to overestimate variability amplitudes and shows pronounced regional dependence. Further analysis suggests that uncertainties in snowfall simulations may be a major source of discrepancies in SSD estimation, although their relative contribution remains uncertain. These findings provide crucial insights for selecting appropriate datasets in snow–climate research and underscore the importance of dataset uncertainty quantification in subseasonal-to-seasonal climate prediction.

title: Orbit Determination and Positioning for Multi-Objective Mars Exploration Mission Using Same-Beam VLBI Tracking
summary: Precise Mars orbiter orbit determination, high-precision lander positioning and planetary interior parameter inversion are core technical requirements for future Mars exploration. The Tianwen-3 Mars sample-return mission requires coordinated orbiter–lander operations, imposing stricter demands on deep-space radio measurements. The Martian tidal Love number k2 describes Mars’ interior structure and tidal response; its accurate estimation constrains the core-mantle configuration and thermal evolution. This study is a simulation-based observability analysis rather than an empirical determination of the Martian tidal parameters. It establishes a joint framework for orbit determination, lander positioning and tidal parameter estimation by integrating ground range-rate and orbiter–lander same-beam VLBI (Very Long Baseline Interferometry) observations. The high-fidelity dynamical models are adopted to build observation models, accounting for the Martian gravity field with degree and order 120, third-body perturbations, solar radiation pressure, relativistic effects and solid tides. Weighted batch least-squares is used to jointly estimate orbiter states, lander coordinates and k2, and the influence of observation arc length on solution accuracy is analyzed. Simulation residuals match preset noise levels. Adding VLBI data reduces the orbiter’s 3D position error by 7.3–33.9%, with an average reduction of approximately 16.8% and full-arc error below 1.6 m. Longer arcs improve lander positioning, reducing 3D error from 88.418 m (7-day) to 33.349 m (45-day). The retrieved k2 0.152866 ± 0.0487 agrees with the reference value of 0.152. However, the current two-station same-beam setup and arc length yield weak empirical constraints on k2, requiring longer observation spans or improved geometries to recover the Martian tidal parameters from real data. Same-beam VLBI provides complementary geometric constraints unavailable from range-rate alone, supporting multi-spacecraft orbit solutions and Martian interior inversion for Tianwen-3.

title: Remote Sensing-Enhanced Geologically Constrained Reinforcement Learning with Dynamic Spatial Search for Mineral Prospectivity Mapping
summary: Mineral prospectivity mapping typically relies on static evaluations of individual research units. Although existing spatial modeling methods capture spatial patterns and relationships, they rarely represent spatial relationships as a sequential process of decision making that depends on the current state. This limits their ability to represent spatial changes and cumulative effects. This study proposes a geologically constrained reinforcement learning framework with dynamic spatial search for mineral prospectivity mapping. The method uses a graph neural network to identify geochemical anomalies. It also integrates favorable geological conditions with surface spectral information to construct a geological environment score. Remote sensing responses further refine the spatial representation and differentiation of favorable geological environments. These scores define an integrated prospectivity field and a local geological constraint that guide an agent to move among neighboring units or stop searching. During inference, each research unit serves as an independent starting state, and its prospectivity is evaluated using both the stop-action value and path-averaged prospectivity generated by the learned policy. The chromite case study in Balikun, Xinjiang, indicates that the proposed method identifies high prospectivity areas showing some spatial correspondence with known deposits and exhibits relatively good predictive performance compared with the selected baseline methods. A comparison with a model that excludes remote sensing information provides case-specific evidence of the contribution of these enhanced geological constraints to prospectivity prioritization when the exploration area is fixed. Ablation analysis and other experiments further support the effectiveness and validity of the proposed method.

title: A Comparative Assessment of Multi-Model Dissolved Organic Matter Absorption Algorithms Using GOCI-II in Korean Coastal Waters
summary: Accurate retrieval of dissolved organic matter absorption at 440 nm (aDOM(440)) remains challenging in optically complex coastal waters. This study evaluated eight empirical algorithms using 203 paired observations of in situ aDOM(440) and remote-sensing reflectance from four marine regions surrounding Korea. Five formulations were recalibrated using Huber regression with a log10-transformed response, while three established algorithms retained published coefficients. The dataset comprised 162 calibration and 41 held-out validation observations. HYB1 achieved the highest calibration R2 (0.416), whereas HYB2 performed best in validation (R2 = 0.500; RMSE = 0.0198 m−1), followed by MR4B (R2 = 0.486; RMSE = 0.0200 m−1). Bootstrap resampling of fixed validation predictions indicated comparatively lower variability in R2 for HYB2 and MR4B, with overlapping confidence intervals.
